The single summary.png contains four bounded panels:

one masked test trial showing true latent paths, known-parameter and selected-tau posterior means, and conditional 95% intervals;
masked-channel and masked-block predictive NLL for known, selected, and wrong-common-timescale GPFA;
negative-condition outcomes and informative-missingness warnings; and
selected timescale, covariance/posterior oracles, poison checks, and interpretation limits.

The caption must state that all posterior intervals condition on fixed parameters, use the full retained trial retrospectively, and omit parameter-selection uncertainty. Smooth curves are not evidence of learned dynamics or mechanism.




Correct known-parameter GPFA should match direct finite Gaussian conditioning and provide calibrated repeated-simulation uncertainty under the primary generator.
A selected grid pair may equal or differ from the generating pair in finite samples. Either outcome is reported without calling the finite grid general parameter recovery.
Static FA and independent-bin inference should recover instantaneous shared structure but cannot interpolate a fully missing time block from neighboring bins.
Independent-channel GP smoothing can interpolate within an observed channel but cannot use other channels to reconstruct a channel hidden for the entire trial.
GPFA can combine cross-channel loading information with temporal covariance for both masks.
The AR(1)/RTS approximation matches one-lag correlation but not the full squared-exponential covariance, so longer-lag and masked-block predictions may differ even when one-step correlations agree.
Wrong common timescale suppresses genuine timescale heterogeneity. Equal true kernels make coordinate-specific latent axes rotationally ambiguous if the observation layer is learned.
Changepoints, correlated residuals, low-rate counts, alignment errors, and informative masks violate different model assumptions and must remain visible rather than tuned away.






Use the primary generator, diagonal \(R\), complete alignment, ignorable masks, and the declared squared-exponential kernels. This is the only primary calibration condition.



Generate a primary latent trial and add
\[
x_1(t)\leftarrow x_1(t)+2\mathbf 1[t\ge0.5]
\]
before applying the observation layer. The squared-exponential prior is misspecified at the abrupt step. Report complete and masked prediction, posterior smoothing across the discontinuity, residual structure, and interval coverage. A smooth bridge is prior-conditioned bias, not evidence that the underlying path was smooth.



Retain the marginal residual variances but use
\[
R_{ij}^{\mathrm{corr}}
=
\sqrt{R_{ii}R_{jj}}\,0.28^{|i-j|}.
\]
The fitted GPFA and FA models still assume diagonal \(R\). Report held-out NLL, cross-channel residual covariance, loading-subspace distortion for learned baselines, latent recovery, and coverage. Do not report diagonal-uniqueness recovery as a valid target.



Set
\[
\lambda_{t,j}
=
\exp\left(operatorname{clip}([Cx_t+d]_j,-1.5,1.1)\right)
\]
and draw
\[
n_{t,j}\sim\operatorname{Poisson}(\lambda_{t,j}).
\]
Analyze
\[
y_{t,j}^{\sqrt{\ }}=\sqrt{n_{t,j}+0.25}
\]
with the bounded Gaussian methods. Rates range approximately from \(0.22\) to \(3.00\) expected counts per bin, so discreteness, skew, and variance dependence remain material. Gaussian NLL and intervals are explicitly labelled approximation diagnostics; no count-likelihood calibration or correction is claimed (Yu et al. 2009).



Set
\[
\tau_1=\tau_2=0.18
\]
with the same unit marginal covariance convention. When \(C\) and kernels are jointly learned, any orthogonal rotation of the two latent coordinates with a corresponding loading rotation preserves the model family. Therefore:

known-\(C\) oracle coordinates remain fixed only by externally supplied \(C\);
learned FA/two-stage/GPFA representatives are scored by the joint two-dimensional loading subspace and optimally aligned path subspace;
coordinate-specific timescale or sign/permutation claims are omitted.

A Procrustes rotation may be estimated from training truth for simulation scoring, frozen, and applied to test paths. It is never used in fitting or parameter selection.



For each trial, draw an offset
\[
\delta_n\in\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}\Delta t.
\]
Generate each latent GP on an extended grid and observe \(x_n(t_m+\delta_n)\), while the analysis labels samples by nominal \(t_m\). Score recovery against the nominal event-relative latent path \(x_n(t_m)\). Because the primary covariance is stationary, a whole-trial shift can leave the marginal observation likelihood nearly unchanged even while event-relative path recovery degrades. This condition therefore tests alignment semantics, not merely covariance fit. No circular wrapping is allowed.



Hide an observation whenever
\[
|y_{t,j}|\ge1.25.
\]
The ordinary row-selection posterior deliberately ignores information carried by the mask. Report missing fraction, latent/observation magnitude inside and outside the mask, and uncorrected posterior RMSE. Coverage and predictive NLL are labelled warning-only under informative missingness and excluded from acceptance. No missingness correction is fabricated.



Use
\[
(\tau_1,\tau_2)=(0.14,0.14)
\]
with known \(C,d,R\). This isolates the cost of incorrectly forcing one common smoothness scale while retaining the same covariance family.



For each latent coordinate, define
\[
\rho_j
=\frac{k_j(t_m,t_{m+1})}{k_j(t_m,t_m)}
=(1-\nu^2)
\exp\left[-\frac{\Delta t^2}{2\tau_j^2}\right].
\]
Use a stationary scalar AR(1)
\[
x_{t+1,j}=\rho_jx_{t,j}+w_{t,j},
\qquad
w_{t,j}\sim\mathcal N(0,1-\rho_j^2),
\]
with the same \(C,d,R\). This matches marginal variance and one-lag covariance but has exponential rather than squared-exponential longer-lag decay. Infer paths with Kalman filtering plus fixed-interval RTS smoothing and compare with direct batch conditioning under the AR covariance (Yu et al. 2009).




The verifier must assert:

Kernel convention: every primary latent Gram matrix has diagonal one, smooth variance \(0.98\), nugget variance \(0.02\), and the declared timescale.
Covariance PSD: all latent, observation, masked-observation, posterior, static-FA, and AR covariances are symmetric within \(10^{-10}\) and have minimum eigenvalue at least \(-10^{-9}\).
Generator algebra: noiseless observations equal \(Cx+d\) exactly within floating-point tolerance.
Split/reset integrity: trials regenerate independently, identifiers are disjoint, and no covariance or posterior block connects different trials.
Mask exclusion: hidden values are absent from conditioning matrices, likelihood contributions, preprocessing, and parameter selection.
No latent leakage: replacing every latent-truth array leaves grid scores, learned baselines, posterior distributions, and observation predictions unchanged.
No test leakage: poisoning all test observations leaves \(C,d,R\) oracle declarations, learned training baselines, grid scores, selected tau, and validation records unchanged.
Grid recomputation: every train and validation marginal NLL is independently recomputed from the declared covariance and the selected pair follows the exact tie rule.
Direct posterior equivalence: covariance-form, precision-form, and generic joint-Gaussian conditioning means/covariances agree within \(10^{-9}\) for complete and masked short trials.
Predictive conditioning equivalence: hidden-observation conditional means/covariances agree with the corresponding blocks of direct joint conditioning.
RTS/batch equivalence: AR(1) Kalman/RTS means, marginal covariances, and adjacent cross-covariances agree with direct AR batch conditioning within \(10^{-9}\).
Static independent-bin limit: setting temporal covariance to identity yields per-time posterior results equal to separate Gaussian conditioning at each bin.
Loading applicability: loading-subspace errors are emitted only for learned static/two-stage methods; known-\(C\) methods are labelled oracle rather than assigned trivial recovery credit.
Alignment scope: sign/permutation or Procrustes transformations are fit using training truth for scoring only, frozen before test scoring, and never affect likelihood or posterior computation.
Equal-kernel guard: coordinate-specific path/tau rows are absent for learned equal-kernel models; joint-subspace metrics remain.
Posterior nesting: masking cannot reduce posterior variance relative to conditioning on the corresponding complete observation set, within numerical tolerance.
Coverage provenance: every coverage row identifies latent versus observation target, complete versus masked region, condition, and fixed parameter source.
Determinism: a clean temporary run produces byte-identical manifest.json, metrics.csv, diagnostics.json, and summary.png.
Metric schema: all keys are unique, labels are nonempty, values are finite, and inapplicable metrics are omitted rather than zero-filled.

These checks verify finite Gaussian calculations and leakage boundaries, not real-data model adequacy.




Nugget added on top of unit signal variance: this silently changes \(k(t,t)\) from one and breaks the declared scale convention.
Bins split across parameter-learning folds: time bins from one trial are dependent and cannot serve as independent train/test units.
Masked targets assimilated before scoring: reconstruction of already observed values is not conditional prediction.
Grid called general maximum likelihood: nine fixed candidates with known \(C,d,R\) are not unrestricted GPFA fitting.
Oracle and selected models merged: known true tau and train/validation-selected tau answer different questions.
Posterior covariance called total uncertainty: it omits uncertainty in selected timescales and learned observation parameters.
Static FA called temporal inference: per-bin posterior calculations do not couple neighboring times.
Two-stage smoothing called GPFA: smoothing observations before static dimensionality reduction solves a different objective.
Independent-channel smoothing credited with cross-channel prediction: a fully hidden channel receives no information from other channels under that baseline.
RTS approximation called the same prior: one-lag agreement does not reproduce squared-exponential higher-lag covariance.
Equal-kernel coordinates scored without rotation allowance: axes within the equal-kernel latent subspace are not uniquely identified when the loading layer is learned.
Poisson square-root scores called calibrated Gaussian probabilities: low counts remain discrete and heteroscedastic.
Correlated residuals forced into factors: apparent shared trajectories may absorb observation-model misspecification.
Informative masks treated as ignorable: the missingness pattern itself carries information.
Alignment jitter ignored: a stationary marginal likelihood can look adequate while event-relative path interpretation is wrong.
Smooth posterior mean called dynamics: covariance-based interpolation is not a learned transition law or mechanism.






For one trial, stack time-major latent and observation vectors. Let
\[
K(\tau_1,\tau_2)\in\mathbb R^{48\times48}
\]
contain the two independent coordinate kernels, and define
\[
\bar C=I_{24}\otimes C,
\quad
\bar d=\mathbf1_{24}\otimes d,
\quad
\bar R=I_{24}\otimes R.
\]
Then
\[
\mathbf y\sim\mathcal N
\left(\bar d,\bar C K\bar C^\top+\bar R\right).
\]
Marginal likelihoods use Cholesky factors and triangular solves, never explicit determinants or inverses.



For observed-entry selector \(H\),
\[
\mathbf y_O=H\mathbf y,
\]
and
\[
\mu_{x\mid O}
=K\bar C_O^\top
(\bar C_OK\bar C_O^\top+\bar R_O)^{-1}
(\mathbf y_O-\bar d_O),
\]
\[
\Sigma_{x\mid O}
=K-K\bar C_O^\top
(\bar C_OK\bar C_O^\top+\bar R_O)^{-1}
\bar C_OK.
\]
This uses the complete retained trial on both sides of a missing block and is retrospective. It is not online filtering.



Partition observed and hidden entries of the marginal Gaussian observation law and compute
\[
p(\mathbf y_H\mid\mathbf y_O,\theta).
\]
Score only hidden values. Report joint predictive NLL, per-entry RMSE, marginal 95% coverage, and average predictive variance. For a whole hidden channel, preserve cross-time covariance in the joint predictive density rather than summing univariate marginals.



Fit bounded two-factor diagonal-noise FA to pooled training time bins, treating bins as independent for fitting. Use six deterministic starts; choose maximal training likelihood, then lower validation NLL and start identifier for ties. Infer each test time independently using the fitted Gaussian factor posterior. This provides no interpolation across a fully hidden time block.
Also compute a known-layer independent-bin oracle using true \(C,d,R\) and \(x_t\sim\mathcal N(0,I_2)\) independently over time. This isolates temporal-prior effects without conflating observation-layer estimation.



Fit one training mean and variance per observed channel, independent across time and channels. It has no latent path. It receives complete and masked observation NLL/RMSE/coverage but no latent recovery or loading-subspace row.



For channel \(i\), use the known marginal covariance
\[
K_i^y
=\sum_{j=1}^2C_{ij}^2K_j+R_{ii}I.
\]
Condition each channel separately on its observed times. This is explicitly labelled a known-marginal independent-channel oracle: it uses true channel covariance but no cross-channel information. It supplies a controlled upper reference for separate smoothing, not a learned real-data method.



Apply the independent-channel smoother to training observations, then fit rank-two PCA and bounded diagonal FA to the smoothed pooled bins. Freeze loadings and apply the same smoother/maps to validation and test trials. Score loading subspace, aligned latent paths, combined observation reconstruction, and masked predictions. These two-stage procedures receive their marginal target through a separate smoother and are not equivalent to joint GPFA.




Known-parameter GPFA oracle: true \(C,d,R,\tau_1,\tau_2,\nu^2\).
Selected-tau GPFA: true \(C,d,R,\nu^2\) plus the frozen train/validation-selected tau pair.
Wrong-common-tau GPFA: true \(C,d,R,\nu^2\) plus \((0.14,0.14)\).

All return exact plug-in path posteriors. Only the first is a true-parameter oracle.



Use the one-lag-matched AR coefficients and process variances above with stationary initial covariance \(I_2\) and true \(C,d,R\). Run independent Kalman filters and fixed-interval RTS smoothers per trial, respecting masks and resets. The smoother is a retrospective inference algorithm for the AR approximation, not a discovered state transition.





Training mean plus diagonal Gaussian. Observation-only independent reference.
Bounded learned static FA. Pooled-bin loading baseline and independent-bin posterior.
Known-layer independent-bin Gaussian posterior. Oracle observation layer without temporal coupling.
Known-marginal independent-channel GP smoothing. Temporal but no cross-channel sharing.
Smoothing-then-PCA. Two-stage learned loading subspace.
Smoothing-then-FA. Two-stage probabilistic loading baseline.
Known-parameter exact GPFA oracle. Correct primary model.
Finite-grid selected-tau GPFA. Known layer, selected covariance prior.
Wrong-common-timescale GPFA. Misspecified smoothness baseline.
One-lag-matched LGSSM/Kalman/RTS. Wrong-family Markov approximation.
Structured negative-condition evaluations. Applicability-limited diagnostics, not new winning methods.






For learned loading basis \(\widehat C\) and true \(C\), report principal angles, maximum angle, RMS sine error, and
\[
\lVert P_{\widehat C}-P_C\rVert_F.
\]
Only static FA/PCA and smoothing-then-FA/PCA receive these rows. Known-layer methods are labelled oracle and do not receive zero-valued “recovery” metrics.



Known-layer GPFA with distinct coordinate-specific kernels retains only the declared sign/permutation conventions. Static PCA/FA and two-stage PCA/FA do not use those distinct temporal kernels and retain a broader orthogonal coordinate ambiguity. For each learned static/two-stage baseline, determine one full orthogonal Procrustes alignment from pooled training estimates and training latent truth, freeze it, transform posterior covariance consistently where coverage is reported, and apply it unchanged to validation/test paths. Do not optimize alignment separately per test trial.
For equal kernels, use one training-fitted orthogonal Procrustes transformation for the joint two-dimensional path and report joint-subspace/path error. Coordinate-specific tau or path claims are not applicable.



Report:

posterior-mean RMSE;
pointwise 95% marginal coverage;
mean posterior variance;
path roughness \(T^{-1}\sum_t\lVert\mu_{t+1}-\mu_t\rVert^2\); and
for temporally masked GPFA/AR posterior paths, block-time versus outside-block RMSE/coverage where emitted.

Full-path Mahalanobis and simultaneous-band diagnostics are useful extensions but are outside this bounded acceptance record; pointwise coverage and covariance-form oracles are retained here.
Coverage is repeated-simulation behavior conditional on fixed parameters. Selected-tau intervals omit timescale-selection uncertainty; learned baseline intervals omit loading-parameter uncertainty.



Report marginal NLL per observed entry on untouched complete test trials for every explicit Gaussian observation model. Static independent-bin methods factor over times; GPFA and AR models use joint within-trial covariance. Poisson stress rows are labelled Gaussian approximation scores.



For each mask region, report joint predictive NLL per hidden entry, RMSE, and marginal 95% coverage for coherent probabilistic prediction methods. Mean predictive variance and hidden count are additionally required for the independent-channel baseline, where they make its fully hidden-channel prior behavior explicit. Separate complete-channel from contiguous-time-block results. Deterministic two-stage PCA/FA reconstructions report hidden-target RMSE only and do not fabricate raw-scale likelihood or coverage.



For the selected grid pair, report selected values, absolute/relative errors, grid rank, train NLL, validation NLL, combined score, and gap to the next candidate. No coordinate-specific timescale recovery is reported in the equal-kernel learned condition.



For applicable Gaussian models, report residual mean and marginal variance, lag-1 autocorrelation, cross-channel residual covariance and maximum off-diagonal magnitude, plus explicit around/outside-changepoint summaries. Cholesky-whitened tails and residual Mahalanobis summaries are outside this bounded acceptance record and remain future extensions.
Residual whiteness under one ordering is a model diagnostic, not proof of the latent mechanism.



Every metrics.csv row contains exactly:
split,condition,method,target,region,metric,value
All values are finite. Inapplicable metrics are omitted and explained in diagnostics.json; warning-only rows include their applicability in method or target labels.




The correct-model oracle tests finite Gaussian inference, not model discovery. The selected-tau baseline tests a tiny predeclared covariance-prior choice while holding the observation layer known. Learned static/two-stage baselines test loading-subspace estimation separately. RTS tests a first-order Markov covariance approximation, not the same squared-exponential prior.
A posterior mean can be smoother than the realized latent path because it averages under a smooth prior. That is expected Bayesian conditioning, not evidence that the method uncovered a transition law. A credible interval conditional on one selected tau pair is not total uncertainty. Better held-out prediction supports one bounded observation/prior combination and does not identify mechanism, dynamics, or unique latent coordinates.






TipLDG synthesis



GPFA specifies covariance among latent values over time; LGSSM specifies a Markov transition and process noise. Both can yield retrospective Gaussian smoothers, but similar posterior plots do not make their model assumptions interchangeable.






It does not discover a transition matrix, vector field, flow, or differential equation from the GP covariance.
It does not make smooth posterior means measured latent trajectories.
It does not make fixed-interval posterior estimates online or causal.
It does not include parameter or model-selection uncertainty in plug-in intervals.
It does not prove a unique loading basis or latent coordinate system.
It does not identify coordinate-specific paths under equal kernels without an external convention.
It does not validate diagonal residuals, Gaussian transformed counts, stationary kernels, or ignorable missingness outside tested conditions.
It does not turn timescale recovery into a biological relaxation constant or mechanism.
It does not infer intrinsic dimension, manifold structure, topology, or nonlinear geometry.
It does not claim universal superiority of GPFA over FA, smoothing, or LGSSM.
It does not call a finite grid unrestricted maximum likelihood.




A real-data use must justify trial boundaries, simultaneity, binning, count transformation, offsets, loading dimension, residual covariance, kernel family, alignment, missingness, parameter sharing, and train/validation/test units. Low counts may require a count likelihood. Correlated residuals may require a richer observation model. Alignment uncertainty, nonstationarity, session drift, and condition changes need explicit models or sensitivity analyses.
Model selection should be nested; posterior calibration should use held-out channels/times/trials; and external behavior should be tested downstream without choosing latent representations on the final test set. Smooth trajectories should be presented with uncertainty and prior sensitivity, not as direct evidence of neural dynamics or mechanism.

mask locations and applicability;

The default command should generate and verify artifacts, with explicit --generate and --verify modes if following the established Phase 3 convention. Verification includes clean temporary regeneration and byte comparison.



The following sources were actually retrieved and inspected. Existing LDG Methods supplied terminology but were not substitutes for source inspection.

Yu et al. (2009): the complete 24-page Journal of Neurophysiology PDF was inspected for the abstract and motivation; two-stage smoothing comparisons; square-root count preprocessing; the GPFA observation model, independent latent GPs, squared-exponential covariance, fixed scale/nugget convention, and EM fitting; the orthonormalized display; comparison with first-order AR/LDS covariance; leave-neuron-out cross-validation; empirical results and discussion; and Appendix equations for the joint Gaussian posterior and EM sufficient statistics. The linked corrigendum was not separately relied upon, and every application figure was not reanalyzed numerically. This source supports the model/inference distinction, trial independence, covariance-prior interpretation, original Gaussian approximation, and predictive evaluation (Yu et al. 2009).
Rasmussen and Williams (2006), Chapter 2: sections 2.2–2.3 and the relevant regression equations were inspected for finite joint Gaussian function values, Gaussian posterior/predictive conditioning, observation noise, and marginal likelihood. Decision-theory and later theoretical sections were not inspected exhaustively (Rasmussen and Williams 2006, ch. 2).

Eigenfunction analysis, structured-input kernels, and exercises were not read in full (Rasmussen and Williams 2006, ch. 4).
Rasmussen and Williams (2006), Chapter 5: sections 5.1–5.4 were inspected for model/hyperparameter selection, marginal-likelihood decomposition, cross-validation, weak lengthscale information in small samples, ridges, and multiple local optima. Classification-specific sections and exercises were not inspected in detail (Rasmussen and Williams 2006, ch. 5).
Cunningham and Yu (2014): the complete 10-page author PDF was inspected for covariance and time-series dimensionality-reduction comparisons, GPFA’s single-trial/noise-model role, and the caution that extracted trajectories reflect the smoothness or dynamical motifs encouraged by the chosen model. Modality examples and references were not read exhaustively (Cunningham and Yu 2014).

The sources do not provide this Toy Model’s dimensions, loading matrix, offsets, residual variances, trial counts, time grid, tau candidates, masks, stress magnitudes, alignment rule, or tolerances. Those are frozen LDG design choices.

Covariance-Prior Trajectories
text:
The latent dimension is \(q=2\), the observed dimension is \(p=6\), and every trial contains \(T=24\) samples on
\[
t_m=\frac{m}{23},
\qquad m=0,\ldots,23.
\]
Whole trials are independent draws. Split sizes are:








Split
Trials
Use

8
fit learned baselines and score the finite timescale grid

test
5

No path continuity, prior covariance, filtering state, or smoother state crosses a trial boundary.



For trial \(n\) and latent coordinate \(j\),
\[
x_j^{(n)}(\cdot)\sim\mathcal{GP}(0,k_j),
\]
independently across \(j\) and \(n\). The true characteristic timescales are
\[
(\tau_1,\tau_2)=(0.08,0.30).
\]
The latent nugget variance is fixed at
\[
\nu^2=0.02,
\]
and marginal variance is fixed at one:
\[
k_j(t,t')
=
(1-\nu^2)
\exp\left[-\frac{(t-t')^2}{2\tau_j^2}\right]
+\nu^2\mathbf 1[t=t'].
\]
Thus \(k_j(t,t)=1\). The smooth signal variance is \(0.98\) and the independent sampled-time latent nugget variance is \(0.02\). The nugget is not observation noise, LGSSM process noise, or parameter uncertainty. Fixing the latent variance removes loading/latent scale ambiguity while retaining sign and permutation ambiguity (Yu et al. 2009).
Every finite Gram matrix is assembled directly on the declared grid and sampled by a deterministic Cholesky factor. Latent draws and observation residuals use independent seed streams.



For each trial and time,
\[
y_t=Cx_t+d+\epsilon_t,
\qquad
\epsilon_t\sim\mathcal N(0,R),
\]
with
\[
C=
\begin{pmatrix}
1.00&0.25\\
0.70&-0.45\\
0.30&0.90\\
-0.65&0.40\\
0.80&0.55\\
-0.25&-0.75
\end{pmatrix},
\]
\[
d=(0.30,-0.20,0.15,0.05,-0.10,0.25)^\top,
\]
and
\[
R=\operatorname{diag}(0.10,0.16,0.22,0.30,0.38,0.48).
\]
The implementation verifies that \(C\) has rank two, records its singular values and condition number, and retains the exact loading subspace \(\operatorname{col}(C)\). Ground-truth latent paths, kernels, and observation parameters enter fitting only for methods explicitly labelled known-parameter oracle.

title: Covariance-Prior Trajectories
Covariance-Prior Trajectories
text:
Correct known-parameter GPFA should match direct finite Gaussian conditioning and provide calibrated repeated-simulation uncertainty under the primary generator.
A selected grid pair may equal or differ from the generating pair in finite samples. Either outcome is reported without calling the finite grid general parameter recovery.
Static FA and independent-bin inference should recover instantaneous shared structure but cannot interpolate a fully missing time block from neighboring bins.
Independent-channel GP smoothing can interpolate within an observed channel but cannot use other channels to reconstruct a channel hidden for the entire trial.
GPFA can combine cross-channel loading information with temporal covariance for both masks.
The AR(1)/RTS approximation matches one-lag correlation but not the full squared-exponential covariance, so longer-lag and masked-block predictions may differ even when one-step correlations agree.
Wrong common timescale suppresses genuine timescale heterogeneity. Equal true kernels make coordinate-specific latent axes rotationally ambiguous if the observation layer is learned.
Changepoints, correlated residuals, low-rate counts, alignment errors, and informative masks violate different model assumptions and must remain visible rather than tuned away.

title: Covariance-Prior Trajectories
text:
Use the primary generator, diagonal \(R\), complete alignment, ignorable masks, and the declared squared-exponential kernels. This is the only primary calibration condition.



Generate a primary latent trial and add
\[
x_1(t)\leftarrow x_1(t)+2\mathbf 1[t\ge0.5]
\]
before applying the observation layer. The squared-exponential prior is misspecified at the abrupt step. Report complete and masked prediction, posterior smoothing across the discontinuity, residual structure, and interval coverage. A smooth bridge is prior-conditioned bias, not evidence that the underlying path was smooth.



Retain the marginal residual variances but use
\[
R_{ij}^{\mathrm{corr}}
=
\sqrt{R_{ii}R_{jj}}\,0.28^{|i-j|}.
\]
The fitted GPFA and FA models still assume diagonal \(R\). Report held-out NLL, cross-channel residual covariance, loading-subspace distortion for learned baselines, latent recovery, and coverage. Do not report diagonal-uniqueness recovery as a valid target.



Set
\[
\lambda_{t,j}
=
\exp\left(operatorname{clip}([Cx_t+d]_j,-1.5,1.1)\right)
\]
and draw
\[
n_{t,j}\sim\operatorname{Poisson}(\lambda_{t,j}).
\]
Analyze
\[
y_{t,j}^{\sqrt{\ }}=\sqrt{n_{t,j}+0.25}
\]
with the bounded Gaussian methods. Rates range approximately from \(0.22\) to \(3.00\) expected counts per bin, so discreteness, skew, and variance dependence remain material. Gaussian NLL and intervals are explicitly labelled approximation diagnostics; no count-likelihood calibration or correction is claimed (Yu et al. 2009).



Set
\[
\tau_1=\tau_2=0.18
\]
with the same unit marginal covariance convention. When \(C\) and kernels are jointly learned, any orthogonal rotation of the two latent coordinates with a corresponding loading rotation preserves the model family. Therefore:

known-\(C\) oracle coordinates remain fixed only by externally supplied \(C\);
learned FA/two-stage/GPFA representatives are scored by the joint two-dimensional loading subspace and optimally aligned path subspace;
coordinate-specific timescale or sign/permutation claims are omitted.

A Procrustes rotation may be estimated from training truth for simulation scoring, frozen, and applied to test paths. It is never used in fitting or parameter selection.



For each trial, draw an offset
\[
\delta_n\in\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}\Delta t.
\]
Generate each latent GP on an extended grid and observe \(x_n(t_m+\delta_n)\), while the analysis labels samples by nominal \(t_m\). Score recovery against the nominal event-relative latent path \(x_n(t_m)\). Because the primary covariance is stationary, a whole-trial shift can leave the marginal observation likelihood nearly unchanged even while event-relative path recovery degrades. This condition therefore tests alignment semantics, not merely covariance fit. No circular wrapping is allowed.



Hide an observation whenever
\[
|y_{t,j}|\ge1.25.
\]
The ordinary row-selection posterior deliberately ignores information carried by the mask. Report missing fraction, latent/observation magnitude inside and outside the mask, and uncorrected posterior RMSE. Coverage and predictive NLL are labelled warning-only under informative missingness and excluded from acceptance. No missingness correction is fabricated.



Use
\[
(\tau_1,\tau_2)=(0.14,0.14)
\]
with known \(C,d,R\). This isolates the cost of incorrectly forcing one common smoothness scale while retaining the same covariance family.



For each latent coordinate, define
\[
\rho_j
=\frac{k_j(t_m,t_{m+1})}{k_j(t_m,t_m)}
=(1-\nu^2)
\exp\left[-\frac{\Delta t^2}{2\tau_j^2}\right].
\]
Use a stationary scalar AR(1)
\[
x_{t+1,j}=\rho_jx_{t,j}+w_{t,j},
\qquad
w_{t,j}\sim\mathcal N(0,1-\rho_j^2),
\]
with the same \(C,d,R\). This matches marginal variance and one-lag covariance but has exponential rather than squared-exponential longer-lag decay. Infer paths with Kalman filtering plus fixed-interval RTS smoothing and compare with direct batch conditioning under the AR covariance (Yu et al. 2009).

title: Covariance-Prior Trajectories
text:
The verifier must assert:

Kernel convention: every primary latent Gram matrix has diagonal one, smooth variance \(0.98\), nugget variance \(0.02\), and the declared timescale.
Covariance PSD: all latent, observation, masked-observation, posterior, static-FA, and AR covariances are symmetric within \(10^{-10}\) and have minimum eigenvalue at least \(-10^{-9}\).
Generator algebra: noiseless observations equal \(Cx+d\) exactly within floating-point tolerance.
Split/reset integrity: trials regenerate independently, identifiers are disjoint, and no covariance or posterior block connects different trials.
Mask exclusion: hidden values are absent from conditioning matrices, likelihood contributions, preprocessing, and parameter selection.
No latent leakage: replacing every latent-truth array leaves grid scores, learned baselines, posterior distributions, and observation predictions unchanged.
No test leakage: poisoning all test observations leaves \(C,d,R\) oracle declarations, learned training baselines, grid scores, selected tau, and validation records unchanged.
Grid recomputation: every train and validation marginal NLL is independently recomputed from the declared covariance and the selected pair follows the exact tie rule.
Direct posterior equivalence: covariance-form, precision-form, and generic joint-Gaussian conditioning means/covariances agree within \(10^{-9}\) for complete and masked short trials.
Predictive conditioning equivalence: hidden-observation conditional means/covariances agree with the corresponding blocks of direct joint conditioning.
RTS/batch equivalence: AR(1) Kalman/RTS means, marginal covariances, and adjacent cross-covariances agree with direct AR batch conditioning within \(10^{-9}\).
Static independent-bin limit: setting temporal covariance to identity yields per-time posterior results equal to separate Gaussian conditioning at each bin.
Loading applicability: loading-subspace errors are emitted only for learned static/two-stage methods; known-\(C\) methods are labelled oracle rather than assigned trivial recovery credit.
Alignment scope: sign/permutation or Procrustes transformations are fit using training truth for scoring only, frozen before test scoring, and never affect likelihood or posterior computation.
Equal-kernel guard: coordinate-specific path/tau rows are absent for learned equal-kernel models; joint-subspace metrics remain.
Posterior nesting: masking cannot reduce posterior variance relative to conditioning on the corresponding complete observation set, within numerical tolerance.
Coverage provenance: every coverage row identifies latent versus observation target, complete versus masked region, condition, and fixed parameter source.
Determinism: a clean temporary run produces byte-identical manifest.json, metrics.csv, diagnostics.json, and summary.png.
Metric schema: all keys are unique, labels are nonempty, values are finite, and inapplicable metrics are omitted rather than zero-filled.

These checks verify finite Gaussian calculations and leakage boundaries, not real-data model adequacy.

title: Covariance-Prior Trajectories
text:
Nugget added on top of unit signal variance: this silently changes \(k(t,t)\) from one and breaks the declared scale convention.
Bins split across parameter-learning folds: time bins from one trial are dependent and cannot serve as independent train/test units.
Masked targets assimilated before scoring: reconstruction of already observed values is not conditional prediction.
Grid called general maximum likelihood: nine fixed candidates with known \(C,d,R\) are not unrestricted GPFA fitting.
Oracle and selected models merged: known true tau and train/validation-selected tau answer different questions.
Posterior covariance called total uncertainty: it omits uncertainty in selected timescales and learned observation parameters.
Static FA called temporal inference: per-bin posterior calculations do not couple neighboring times.
Two-stage smoothing called GPFA: smoothing observations before static dimensionality reduction solves a different objective.
Independent-channel smoothing credited with cross-channel prediction: a fully hidden channel receives no information from other channels under that baseline.
RTS approximation called the same prior: one-lag agreement does not reproduce squared-exponential higher-lag covariance.
Equal-kernel coordinates scored without rotation allowance: axes within the equal-kernel latent subspace are not uniquely identified when the loading layer is learned.
Poisson square-root scores called calibrated Gaussian probabilities: low counts remain discrete and heteroscedastic.
Correlated residuals forced into factors: apparent shared trajectories may absorb observation-model misspecification.
Informative masks treated as ignorable: the missingness pattern itself carries information.
Alignment jitter ignored: a stationary marginal likelihood can look adequate while event-relative path interpretation is wrong.
Smooth posterior mean called dynamics: covariance-based interpolation is not a learned transition law or mechanism.

title: Covariance-Prior Trajectories
text:
For one trial, stack time-major latent and observation vectors. Let
\[
K(\tau_1,\tau_2)\in\mathbb R^{48\times48}
\]
contain the two independent coordinate kernels, and define
\[
\bar C=I_{24}\otimes C,
\quad
\bar d=\mathbf1_{24}\otimes d,
\quad
\bar R=I_{24}\otimes R.
\]
Then
\[
\mathbf y\sim\mathcal N
\left(\bar d,\bar C K\bar C^\top+\bar R\right).
\]
Marginal likelihoods use Cholesky factors and triangular solves, never explicit determinants or inverses.



For observed-entry selector \(H\),
\[
\mathbf y_O=H\mathbf y,
\]
and
\[
\mu_{x\mid O}
=K\bar C_O^\top
(\bar C_OK\bar C_O^\top+\bar R_O)^{-1}
(\mathbf y_O-\bar d_O),
\]
\[
\Sigma_{x\mid O}
=K-K\bar C_O^\top
(\bar C_OK\bar C_O^\top+\bar R_O)^{-1}
\bar C_OK.
\]
This uses the complete retained trial on both sides of a missing block and is retrospective. It is not online filtering.



Partition observed and hidden entries of the marginal Gaussian observation law and compute
\[
p(\mathbf y_H\mid\mathbf y_O,\theta).
\]
Score only hidden values. Report joint predictive NLL, per-entry RMSE, marginal 95% coverage, and average predictive variance. For a whole hidden channel, preserve cross-time covariance in the joint predictive density rather than summing univariate marginals.



Fit bounded two-factor diagonal-noise FA to pooled training time bins, treating bins as independent for fitting. Use six deterministic starts; choose maximal training likelihood, then lower validation NLL and start identifier for ties. Infer each test time independently using the fitted Gaussian factor posterior. This provides no interpolation across a fully hidden time block.
Also compute a known-layer independent-bin oracle using true \(C,d,R\) and \(x_t\sim\mathcal N(0,I_2)\) independently over time. This isolates temporal-prior effects without conflating observation-layer estimation.



Fit one training mean and variance per observed channel, independent across time and channels. It has no latent path. It receives complete and masked observation NLL/RMSE/coverage but no latent recovery or loading-subspace row.



For channel \(i\), use the known marginal covariance
\[
K_i^y
=\sum_{j=1}^2C_{ij}^2K_j+R_{ii}I.
\]
Condition each channel separately on its observed times. This is explicitly labelled a known-marginal independent-channel oracle: it uses true channel covariance but no cross-channel information. It supplies a controlled upper reference for separate smoothing, not a learned real-data method.



Apply the independent-channel smoother to training observations, then fit rank-two PCA and bounded diagonal FA to the smoothed pooled bins. Freeze loadings and apply the same smoother/maps to validation and test trials. Score loading subspace, aligned latent paths, combined observation reconstruction, and masked predictions. These two-stage procedures receive their marginal target through a separate smoother and are not equivalent to joint GPFA.




Known-parameter GPFA oracle: true \(C,d,R,\tau_1,\tau_2,\nu^2\).
Selected-tau GPFA: true \(C,d,R,\nu^2\) plus the frozen train/validation-selected tau pair.
Wrong-common-tau GPFA: true \(C,d,R,\nu^2\) plus \((0.14,0.14)\).

All return exact plug-in path posteriors. Only the first is a true-parameter oracle.



Use the one-lag-matched AR coefficients and process variances above with stationary initial covariance \(I_2\) and true \(C,d,R\). Run independent Kalman filters and fixed-interval RTS smoothers per trial, respecting masks and resets. The smoother is a retrospective inference algorithm for the AR approximation, not a discovered state transition.

title: Covariance-Prior Trajectories
text:
Training mean plus diagonal Gaussian. Observation-only independent reference.
Bounded learned static FA. Pooled-bin loading baseline and independent-bin posterior.
Known-layer independent-bin Gaussian posterior. Oracle observation layer without temporal coupling.
Known-marginal independent-channel GP smoothing. Temporal but no cross-channel sharing.
Smoothing-then-PCA. Two-stage learned loading subspace.
Smoothing-then-FA. Two-stage probabilistic loading baseline.
Known-parameter exact GPFA oracle. Correct primary model.

One-lag-matched LGSSM/Kalman/RTS. Wrong-family Markov approximation.
Structured negative-condition evaluations. Applicability-limited diagnostics, not new winning methods.

title: Covariance-Prior Trajectories
text:
For learned loading basis \(\widehat C\) and true \(C\), report principal angles, maximum angle, RMS sine error, and
\[
\lVert P_{\widehat C}-P_C\rVert_F.
\]
Only static FA/PCA and smoothing-then-FA/PCA receive these rows. Known-layer methods are labelled oracle and do not receive zero-valued “recovery” metrics.



Known-layer GPFA with distinct coordinate-specific kernels retains only the declared sign/permutation conventions. Static PCA/FA and two-stage PCA/FA do not use those distinct temporal kernels and retain a broader orthogonal coordinate ambiguity. For each learned static/two-stage baseline, determine one full orthogonal Procrustes alignment from pooled training estimates and training latent truth, freeze it, transform posterior covariance consistently where coverage is reported, and apply it unchanged to validation/test paths. Do not optimize alignment separately per test trial.
For equal kernels, use one training-fitted orthogonal Procrustes transformation for the joint two-dimensional path and report joint-subspace/path error. Coordinate-specific tau or path claims are not applicable.



Report:

posterior-mean RMSE;
pointwise 95% marginal coverage;
mean posterior variance;
path roughness \(T^{-1}\sum_t\lVert\mu_{t+1}-\mu_t\rVert^2\); and
for temporally masked GPFA/AR posterior paths, block-time versus outside-block RMSE/coverage where emitted.

Full-path Mahalanobis and simultaneous-band diagnostics are useful extensions but are outside this bounded acceptance record; pointwise coverage and covariance-form oracles are retained here.
Coverage is repeated-simulation behavior conditional on fixed parameters. Selected-tau intervals omit timescale-selection uncertainty; learned baseline intervals omit loading-parameter uncertainty.



Report marginal NLL per observed entry on untouched complete test trials for every explicit Gaussian observation model. Static independent-bin methods factor over times; GPFA and AR models use joint within-trial covariance. Poisson stress rows are labelled Gaussian approximation scores.



For each mask region, report joint predictive NLL per hidden entry, RMSE, and marginal 95% coverage for coherent probabilistic prediction methods. Mean predictive variance and hidden count are additionally required for the independent-channel baseline, where they make its fully hidden-channel prior behavior explicit. Separate complete-channel from contiguous-time-block results. Deterministic two-stage PCA/FA reconstructions report hidden-target RMSE only and do not fabricate raw-scale likelihood or coverage.



For the selected grid pair, report selected values, absolute/relative errors, grid rank, train NLL, validation NLL, combined score, and gap to the next candidate. No coordinate-specific timescale recovery is reported in the equal-kernel learned condition.



For applicable Gaussian models, report residual mean and marginal variance, lag-1 autocorrelation, cross-channel residual covariance and maximum off-diagonal magnitude, plus explicit around/outside-changepoint summaries. Cholesky-whitened tails and residual Mahalanobis summaries are outside this bounded acceptance record and remain future extensions.
Residual whiteness under one ordering is a model diagnostic, not proof of the latent mechanism.



Every metrics.csv row contains exactly:
split,condition,method,target,region,metric,value
All values are finite. Inapplicable metrics are omitted and explained in diagnostics.json; warning-only rows include their applicability in method or target labels.

title: Covariance-Prior Trajectories
text:
The correct-model oracle tests finite Gaussian inference, not model discovery. The selected-tau baseline tests a tiny predeclared covariance-prior choice while holding the observation layer known. Learned static/two-stage baselines test loading-subspace estimation separately. RTS tests a first-order Markov covariance approximation, not the same squared-exponential prior.
A posterior mean can be smoother than the realized latent path because it averages under a smooth prior. That is expected Bayesian conditioning, not evidence that the method uncovered a transition law. A credible interval conditional on one selected tau pair is not total uncertainty. Better held-out prediction supports one bounded observation/prior combination and does not identify mechanism, dynamics, or unique latent coordinates.






TipLDG synthesis



GPFA specifies covariance among latent values over time; LGSSM specifies a Markov transition and process noise. Both can yield retrospective Gaussian smoothers, but similar posterior plots do not make their model assumptions interchangeable.

title: Covariance-Prior Trajectories
text:
It does not discover a transition matrix, vector field, flow, or differential equation from the GP covariance.
It does not make smooth posterior means measured latent trajectories.
It does not make fixed-interval posterior estimates online or causal.
It does not include parameter or model-selection uncertainty in plug-in intervals.
It does not prove a unique loading basis or latent coordinate system.
It does not identify coordinate-specific paths under equal kernels without an external convention.
It does not validate diagonal residuals, Gaussian transformed counts, stationary kernels, or ignorable missingness outside tested conditions.
It does not turn timescale recovery into a biological relaxation constant or mechanism.
It does not infer intrinsic dimension, manifold structure, topology, or nonlinear geometry.
It does not claim universal superiority of GPFA over FA, smoothing, or LGSSM.
It does not call a finite grid unrestricted maximum likelihood.

title: Covariance-Prior Trajectories
text:
A real-data use must justify trial boundaries, simultaneity, binning, count transformation, offsets, loading dimension, residual covariance, kernel family, alignment, missingness, parameter sharing, and train/validation/test units. Low counts may require a count likelihood. Correlated residuals may require a richer observation model. Alignment uncertainty, nonstationarity, session drift, and condition changes need explicit models or sensitivity analyses.
Model selection should be nested; posterior calibration should use held-out channels/times/trials; and external behavior should be tested downstream without choosing latent representations on the final test set. Smooth trajectories should be presented with uncertainty and prior sensitivity, not as direct evidence of neural dynamics or mechanism.

title: Toy Models
text:
Toy Models connect explicit questions and known generative structure to simulation, recovery, evaluation, and interpretation limits.

Two-Dimensional Autonomous Dynamics: Generation and Recovery — an executable, known-ground-truth comparison of cubic vector-field recovery, an affine baseline, and a derivative-permutation control. (L1, stable)

Label-Dependent Demixing — a supervised time × stimulus × decision Toy Model comparing marginal means, PCA, marginal PCA, regularized dPCA, decoding, label shuffles, missing cells, pseudo-populations, and mean-versus-single-trial transfer. (L1, stable)

title: Linear-Gaussian Inference Ladder
text:
This L1/stable object is the scientific and reproducibility record for the first Phase 3 generation/recovery vertical slice. It deliberately separates a known simulator, exact inference conditional on fixed parameters, finite-grid parameter selection, predictive scoring, latent-state recovery, and stress tests. Reported numerical values are deterministic outputs of the bounded implementation under master seed 20260819; they are not inferred from the equations or generalized beyond this simulator.
Assumed background: scalar Gaussian conditioning, conditional expectation, covariance, and elementary time-series evaluation. The stable prerequisite Method Objects fix LDG terminology, but they are not substitutes for the external-source inspection recorded in Evidence inspected.


For a scalar discrete-time linear-Gaussian state-space model (LGSSM) with retained latent ground truth:

do a known-parameter Kalman filter, a known-parameter fixed-interval Rauch–Tung–Striebel (RTS) smoother, and direct batch Gaussian conditioning return the same model-conditional posterior marginals under their respective information sets;
how do online prediction, online filtering, and retrospective smoothing differ from latent recovery and from observation prediction;
how much performance and calibration change when parameters are selected from a finite grid rather than supplied by the generator; and
how do wrong noise ratios, a contiguous missing block, a false sequence boundary, near-unit-root dynamics, and informative missingness expose model or interpretation failures?

The primary acceptance question is numerical and inferential correctness under the declared model. It is not whether the recovered mean merely looks smooth.



For each independent sequence, the retained scalar latent state is (z_{1:T}), the observed scalar is (x_{1:T}), and the complete-data generator is
\[
z_1\sim\mathcal N(0,p_1),
\qquad
p_1=\frac{q}{1-a^2},
\]
\[
z_{t+1}=a z_t+w_t,
\qquad
w_t\overset{\mathrm{iid}}\sim\mathcal N(0,q),
\]
\[
x_t=z_t+v_t,
\qquad
v_t\overset{\mathrm{iid}}\sim\mathcal N(0,r),
\]
with (z_1), all (w_t), and all (v_t) mutually independent. The primary parameters are fixed before simulation:
\[
a=0.85,
\qquad
q=0.10,
\qquad
r=0.40,
\qquad
p_1=\frac{0.10}{1-0.85^2}.
\]
The initialization is the stationary zero-mean law for this scalar stable model. Stationarity is a property of the declared generator and initialization, not a conclusion inferred from a finite simulated trace.
The observation map is the identity. This removes latent-coordinate ambiguity for this bounded scalar recovery test, but it does not make the latent state directly observed: (x_t) still contains independent measurement noise. Retaining (z_t) for scoring is a simulation privilege. Test latent truth is never an input to parameter selection, filtering, smoothing, or batch conditioning.



Generation, masking, parameter selection, inference, and scoring are separate stages with separate function boundaries in the implementation.

Generate complete sequences. For every sequence, draw a fresh (z_1), process-noise stream, and observation-noise stream from its split-specific random generator. Store the latent and complete observation arrays before applying any mask.
Assign immutable sequence boundaries. Train, validation, and test sequences are independent replicates. Every recovery method starts each sequence from the declared prior; no posterior mean or covariance crosses a true boundary.
Create masks without changing the complete arrays. The primary complete-data mask retains every observation. The missing-block mask removes a predeclared contiguous interval only on test copies. The informative-missingness negative control derives a separate observation-magnitude-dependent mask from the frozen test observations and is never treated as ignorable evidence.
Select parameters without latent truth. The finite grid reads only train and validation observations, masks, and sequence boundaries. It may use innovation likelihood, but no latent state or test quantity.
Run recovery. Known-parameter and selected-parameter methods receive observations, masks, boundaries, and their declared parameter tuple.
Score last. Latent truth is joined only after all posterior and predictive outputs have been frozen.

This ordering prevents generation from being mistaken for recovery and prevents test latent states from becoming pseudo-observations.

The implementation uses NumPy Generator(PCG64(SeedSequence(words))) with distinct split and sequence words. Any change to these values is a contract change, not routine tuning. No primary-parameter correction was required.



The learned-parameter variant is a bounded plug-in baseline over the 27 predeclared tuples
\[
a\in\{0.75,0.85,0.95\},
\qquad
q\in\{0.05,0.10,0.20\},
\qquad
r\in\{0.20,0.40,0.80\}.
\]
For every tuple, each sequence is reset to (m_1=0) and the tuple’s stationary variance (q/(1-a^2)). Selection minimizes the sum of the mean train and mean validation one-step innovation negative log likelihood. Test observations, test latent truth, and all test metrics remain unavailable until one tuple is frozen. Exact ties are broken lexicographically by ((a,q,r)), not by distance to the true parameters.
This is finite-grid model selection over a declared candidate set. It is not a claim of unrestricted LGSSM maximum-likelihood estimation, consistency, or parameter-identification. Särkkä distinguishes known-parameter state inference from parameter inference and gives the prediction-error factorization of the marginal likelihood used here as a scoring rule (Särkkä 2013, ch. 12, especially sec. 12.1).

The wrong-(q/r) conditions alter inference only; their data remain the primary generator. The near-unit-root condition is a separate generated data set of four sequences of length (T=160), using the dedicated stage word 40. It is evaluated once with its matched stationary prior and once with a deliberately tight prior variance 0.05. It is not pooled into primary success criteria.




The implementation must use the existing Python/NumPy runtime and must not install a dependency. For each split, generation is vectorized across independent sequences only where this does not obscure resets. Stored arrays preserve a sequence axis; flattening sequences before inference is prohibited except in the explicit reset-boundary negative control.
The generator retains (z) and (x) with split and sequence identities. Recovery functions receive observations, masks, boundaries, and parameters rather than the latent array. Computed poison diagnostics change test observations or every latent array and verify that grid selection and recovery outputs remain unchanged; separate-sequence invocation is also compared numerically with the stacked multi-sequence path. Retained latent values enter only the later scoring functions.


Let
\[
\mathcal I_t^{\mathrm{F}}=\sigma(x_s:\ s\le t,\ x_s\text{ observed})
\]
be the online information set. Before observing (x_t), the scalar prediction is
\[
m_{t\mid t-1}=a m_{t-1\mid t-1},
\qquad
p_{t\mid t-1}=a^2p_{t-1\mid t-1}+q,
\]
with (m_{1}=0) and (p_{1}=p_1). For an observed (x_t),
\[
\nu_t=x_t-m_{t\mid t-1},
\qquad
s_t=p_{t\mid t-1}+r,
\qquad
k_t=\frac{p_{t\mid t-1}}{s_t},
\]
\[
m_{t\mid t}=m_{t\mid t-1}+k_t\nu_t,
\qquad
p_{t\mid t}=p_{t\mid t-1}-k_t^2s_t.
\]
These are the scalar specialization of exact linear-Gaussian Bayesian filtering (Kalman 1960; Särkkä 2013, theorem 4.2). If (x_t) is missing, no pseudo-observation is inserted:
\[
m_{t\mid t}=m_{t\mid t-1},
\qquad
p_{t\mid t}=p_{t\mid t-1}.
\]
Thus a filter traverses the declared missing block by repeated open-loop prediction. It cannot use observations after the current time.



Let
\[
\mathcal I_T^{\mathrm{S}}=\sigma(x_s:\ 1\le s\le T,\ x_s\text{ observed})
\]
be the retrospective information set. Starting from (m_{TT},p_{TT}), the scalar RTS recursion is
\[
j_t=\frac{p_{t\mid t}a}{p_{t+1\mid t}},
\]
\[
m_{t\mid T}=m_{t\mid t}+j_t\left(m_{t+1\mid T}-m_{t+1\mid t}\right),
\]
\[
p_{t\mid T}=p_{t\mid t}+j_t^2\left(p_{t+1\mid T}-p_{t+1\mid t}\right).
\]
Rauch, Tung, and Striebel derive the backward recursion from the forward filtering solution; the modern Bayesian statement makes explicit that it computes (p(z_tx_{1:T})), whereas filtering computes (p(z_tx_{1:t})) (Rauch et al. 1965, sec. 3.2; Särkkä 2013, secs. 8.1–8.2). Later observations may therefore revise states inside the missing block. That revision is valid only retrospectively and must never be described as information available online at time (t).



For a bounded sequence, construct the prior path mean (m_z=0) and covariance (K_z) from the declared prior and transition recursion. Under the stationary primary model,
\[
(K_z)_{ij}=p_1 a^{|i-j|}.
\]
For observed time indices (O), let (H_O) select those state coordinates and let (x_O) be the corresponding observation vector. Direct conditioning gives
\[
\mu_{z\mid x_O}
=m_z+K_zH_O^\top
\left(H_OK_zH_O^\top+rI\right)^{-1}
(x_O-H_Om_z),
\]
\[
\Sigma_{z\mid x_O}
=K_z-K_zH_O^\top
\left(H_OK_zH_O^\top+rI\right)^{-1}
H_OK_z.
\]
The implementation must use a linear solve, not an explicit matrix inverse. For each short oracle sequence, conditioning on observations through (t) supplies the current-time filter oracle, while conditioning on every observed time through (T) supplies the full smoother oracle. Agreement with this independently assembled joint Gaussian is an implementation test, not an additional estimator (Särkkä 2013, secs. 4.1–4.3, 8.1–8.2).




Exactly one composite summary.png is allowed. It must have a scientific checking purpose and contain no decorative panels:

one predeclared test sequence with latent truth, observations, filter mean, smoother mean, and filter 95% model-conditional intervals;
the same sequence with the missing block visibly marked;
numerical oracle and leakage summaries; and
compact metric and failure-diagnostic panels distinguishing known parameters, selected parameters, wrong-(q/r), reset, near-unit-root, and informative-missingness stresses.

The caption must state that the smoother is retrospective and that the intervals condition on fixed parameters. Visual overlap, smoothness, or a compelling trajectory is never an acceptance oracle.



These are model-derived expectations, not prefilled empirical results.

In exact arithmetic under the correct fixed model, recursive filtering and smoothing should equal direct Gaussian conditioning for the same observations and information set (Särkkä 2013, theorems 4.2 and 8.2).
Under the exact fixed model, (p_{tT}p_{tt}) because smoothing conditions on a superset of observations. Floating-point violations beyond tolerance indicate an implementation problem, not negative variance.
Under the correct generator, posterior means are conditional-MSE-optimal for their own information sets. Across repeated draws, the smoother can have lower expected latent MSE than the filter, but any finite test realization may deviate. Lower smoothing RMSE does not make smoothing suitable for an online task.
During a missing block, the filter mean and variance evolve only through the transition. The smoother may revise that interval using later observations, but only after the interval endpoint is available.
Wrong (q/r) changes gains, innovation variance, posterior width, and retrospective coupling. The direction and size of finite-sample metric changes are empirical outputs, not guaranteed numerical values.
Near (a=1), stationary variance and long-horizon predictive uncertainty are larger and initialization effects can persist. This stress is reported separately rather than used to redefine primary success.






Use the true tuple for filtering, smoothing, prediction, and batch conditioning. This condition tests exact-inference implementation and finite-sample recovery separately:

batch-versus-recursion discrepancies test numerical implementation;
latent RMSE and coverage test recovery under one realized sample from the declared correct model; and
predictive negative log likelihood and innovations test the observation distribution.

Low RMSE is not required for posterior correctness on every realization, because process and observation noise leave irreducible uncertainty.



Apply q_small_r_large and q_large_r_small to the unchanged primary test observations. Score predictive likelihood, filter and smoother latent RMSE, interval coverage, mean posterior variance, standardized innovation variance, and lag-1 autocorrelation. These are plug-in, misspecified posteriors. Their intervals do not become valid uncertainty statements about the true generator merely because the covariance recursion remains algebraically valid.



Remove zero-based observations (x_{30:45}) from every primary test sequence before both forward and backward inference. Score missing-block and observed-region errors separately. Innovation likelihood is computed only where observations are available. The filter’s block trajectory is an online prediction from pre-block information; the smoother’s block trajectory is a retrospective reconstruction using both sides. Comparing their RMSE must preserve that information-set difference.



Take the first two independently generated primary test sequences and, only for this negative control, concatenate them without resetting the prior at the join. Run the same parameter tuple as though the join were a real transition. Compare against correct separate-sequence inference using the inherited boundary prediction, first-state estimate difference, artificial-continuity magnitude, and proper-versus-joined RMSE over the first eight states of the second sequence.
The intended demonstration is that carrying a posterior across an independent reset can impose artificial continuity or otherwise distort inference near the join. The realized direction and magnitude are reported, not guaranteed. The negative control must never alter ordinary split handling.



Generate the separate (a=0.99) condition and compare matched-stationary versus tight-variance initialization. Report stationary prior variance, maximum filter and smoother variance, first-20-step mean/variance sensitivity, and covariance finiteness/nonnegativity. In addition, propagate variance without observations to fixed horizons (h{1,10,50,100,200}) under both initializations. This diagnostic separates long-horizon predictive uncertainty from posterior variance under continuous measurement updates. It is not a second primary model and cannot rescue a failed primary oracle.



For a warning-only negative control, hide an observation whenever (|x_t|>0.9). The ordinary skipped-update filter and smoother deliberately ignore the information carried by that observation-dependent mask. The posterior target under a joint observation–missingness model is therefore not the same as conditioning only on retained values. The resulting missing fraction, latent magnitude inside/outside the mask, and skipped-update filter RMSE are labeled uncorrected informative-missingness stress, excluded from primary acceptance, and used only to show why an ignorable-missingness interpretation fails. No correction or calibrated uncertainty claim is permitted without explicitly modeling the missingness process.




The implementation and generated diagnostics must assert all of the following.

Filter batch equivalence: for every short oracle prefix and observed mask, the recursive (m_{tt},p_{tt}) equal the current-time marginal from direct conditioning on observations through (t).
Smoother batch equivalence: all short-sequence (m_{tT},p_{tT}) equal the corresponding full batch posterior marginals.
Nested-information variance: (p_{tT}p_{tt}+10^{-12}) for the regular correct-model computations.
No look-ahead: changing (x_{t+1:T}) while holding (x_{1:t}) fixed cannot change any stored filter output through (t); it may change smoother outputs.
No latent leakage: parameter selection and inference inputs contain no latent array, and test latent truth is joined only by the scoring stage.
Boundary reset: separate-sequence outputs equal outputs obtained by running each sequence independently; only the named negative control omits the reset.
Numerical covariance: assembled batch covariances are symmetric within (10^{-12}); all scalar variances are at least (-10^{-12}); oracle mean and variance discrepancies are at most (10^{-10}) in absolute value.
Missing-block handling: no innovation or likelihood contribution is emitted at hidden times, and skipped updates equal predictions exactly within floating-point tolerance.
Determinism: two clean executions with the same runtime and command produce byte-identical manifest.json, metrics.csv, diagnostics.json, and summary.png.
Metric provenance: every metrics row identifies split, condition, parameter source, method, inference target, region, metric, and value.

Tolerance values belong in the manifest. Passing structural checks does not establish scientific model adequacy.




Filter reads the future: any dependence of a filter output at (t) on (x_{t+1:T}) is leakage and a hard failure.
Smoother mislabeled online: a retrospective estimate presented as available at time (t) is an inferential failure even if its arithmetic is correct.
Batch disagreement: discrepancies above tolerance under the same fixed model indicate indexing, covariance, masking, or conditioning errors.
Latent truth enters selection: any grid criterion, preprocessing decision, or posterior conditioned on (z_t) invalidates the learned-parameter comparison.
State propagates across true boundaries: failure to reset invents dependence between independent sequences.
Wrong-noise certainty interpreted as calibrated: covariance is conditional on the assumed tuple; misspecified plug-in intervals can be narrow and wrong.
Parameter uncertainty omitted silently: selected-grid posterior intervals exclude uncertainty over the selection procedure and candidate tuple.
Missingness treated as ignorable without justification: state-dependent absence changes the conditioning problem.
Near-unit-root results pooled with primary results: doing so changes the acceptance population and obscures initialization sensitivity.
Plausible figure replaces numerical checks: visual smoothness cannot verify a posterior, a boundary, or calibration.
Recovery treated as mechanism: successful state estimation in a simulator does not establish a causal or biological transition law.




The recovery outputs are kept distinct.


For observed times, the one-step observation predictive law is
\[
x_t\mid x_{1:t-1}\sim
\mathcal N(m_{t\mid t-1},s_t),
\qquad
s_t=p_{t\mid t-1}+r.
\]
The held-out one-step negative log likelihood and standardized innovation (_t/) score this observation prediction. Smoothing does not produce a new prospective sequence likelihood; the same forward predictive factorization supplies the fixed-parameter likelihood (Särkkä 2013, sec. 12.1.1).



Filter and smoother posterior means are scored against retained (z_t) only after inference. Filtering RMSE evaluates online recovery; smoothing RMSE evaluates retrospective recovery. They are different tasks because their conditioning sigma-fields differ.



Pointwise 95% coverage uses
\[
m\pm 1.959963984540054\sqrt{p}
\]
for the relevant filter or smoother posterior. Coverage is aggregated across independent test sequences and time points, with missing-block inside/outside records. It describes repeated-simulation behavior under a fixed assumed tuple. A single interval does not carry a frequentist guarantee for one state, and finite-sample aggregate coverage need not equal 0.95 exactly.



Known-parameter intervals condition on the true tuple. Selected-grid intervals condition on one frozen selected tuple. Neither integrates over parameter uncertainty. The learned-versus-known gap is reported in prediction, recovery, and coverage metrics, but no plug-in covariance is called total uncertainty.





Stationary-mean reference. Use the generator’s zero stationary mean as a deliberately non-temporal latent point reference. No latent posterior coverage is reported.
Persistence / last observation. Use a latent point proxy equal to the most recent observed (x); before any observation use zero. It has no model-conditional state interval.
Open-loop state prediction. Assimilate the first available observation once using the declared model, then propagate without further updates. It is a bounded no-reassimilation baseline; prediction-only propagation inside a missing block is also the filter’s exact behavior conditional on its last filtered state.
Known-parameter Kalman filter. Compute online predictive and filtering distributions using only data through the current time (Kalman 1960; Särkkä 2013, ch. 4).
Known-parameter RTS smoother. Run the fixed-interval backward pass after the complete declared interval is available (Rauch et al. 1965; Särkkä 2013, ch. 8).
Direct batch Gaussian conditioning. Use only bounded short sequences as an independently assembled correctness oracle.
Selected-grid filter and smoother. Freeze the finite-grid tuple selected by train/validation innovation likelihood, then evaluate on untouched test sequences.

Static Factor Analysis is a conceptual prerequisite and order-blind comparison, not an executable candidate in this scalar unit. It cannot represent the transition or distinguish online from retrospective information merely because factor scores happen to be smooth.



Every metrics row includes:
split, condition, parameter_source, method, inference_target,
region, metric, value
Required metrics are:

held-out one-step predictive negative log likelihood at observed test times;
filtering latent RMSE and smoothing latent RMSE;
pointwise 95% posterior interval coverage;
innovation mean, variance, and lag-1 autocorrelation, using standardized innovations for calibration summaries;
mean filtering variance and mean smoothing variance;
maximum absolute batch-versus-recursion mean and variance discrepancy;
missing-block inside and outside RMSE/coverage;
wrong-parameter stress metrics;
selected-grid versus known-parameter gaps; and
reset-boundary predictive and local-recovery diagnostics.

Train and validation likelihood rows used for selection remain distinct from test evaluation rows. Metrics that do not apply are omitted rather than coerced to zero. In particular, baselines without a latent posterior have no coverage row, and smoothing has no separate prospective one-step likelihood row.


These values are read from the generated manifest.json, metrics.csv, and diagnostics.json; they remain conditional on this implementation and fixed random seed.

The selected-grid prediction, recovery, and coverage gaps are zero here because the finite grid selected the generating tuple. This favorable finite-sample outcome is not a general parameter-learning result. The smoother’s lower RMSE uses later observations and is not an online comparison. Both wrong-noise conditions degraded RMSE and interval coverage, while the reset negative control imposed a nonzero inherited boundary prediction. In the near-unit stress, a tight initial variance approached the model’s stationary variance slowly under open-loop propagation; this is a diagnostic of the declared (a=0.99) model, not a universal unit-root effect size.




The passed correct-model oracle establishes that, for the declared scalar LGSSM and numerical tolerance, the implementation returns the same fixed-parameter Gaussian marginals by recursive and batch routes. Recovery metrics would then describe finite simulations from that generator. They would not establish that any real data source is linear, Gaussian, stationary, first-order Markov, correctly segmented, or governed by the recovered transition.
Filtering and smoothing must remain separate in every table and caption. The filter answers an online question with (x_{1:t}); the smoother answers a retrospective question with (x_{1:T}). More information can improve retrospective state reconstruction without making the smoother a fair competitor for a prospective decision.
Wrong-(q/r), missing-block, boundary, and near-unit-root conditions diagnose sensitivity to assumptions. They do not provide a generic ranking of all state-space methods. A selected grid point is one data-dependent plug-in model among 27 candidates, not recovered ground truth.




It does not prove that observed data lie on a manifold or possess non-Euclidean geometry.
It does not identify a causal, physical, neural, or biological state.
It does not show that temporal correlation is a mechanistic dynamical law.
It does not turn decoding or latent RMSE into evidence of representation.
It does not prove unrestricted parameter identifiability or successful maximum-likelihood learning.
It does not include parameter uncertainty in plug-in posterior intervals.
It does not make fixed-interval smoothing online, causal, or prospectively available.
It does not validate skipped updates under informative missingness.
It does not imply that low reconstruction error, nominal coverage, or a smooth plot is sufficient evidence for model adequacy.
It does not authorize extension to another Phase 3 candidate or promotion to stable.




Before a real-data use, the analyst would need to justify observation units, sampling intervals, sequence resets, covariates, latent dimension, transition and noise structure, missingness, nonstationarity, and evaluation splits. Parameters and preprocessing must be learned on independent training units. Prospective tasks require filtering or forecasting; retrospective smoothing outputs cannot be backdated into an online analysis. Residual and predictive checks should test Gaussianity, white innovations, heteroscedasticity, regime changes, and boundary effects. None of those extensions is executed here.





The implementation owner may create only:

The source script must regenerate every artifact from scratch. The manifest records equations, all seeds, split sizes, sequence lengths, parameter grid and tie rule, selected tuple, missing-block indices, stress definitions, runtime and package versions, numerical tolerances, generation command, verification command, and SHA-256 hashes. metrics.csv contains tidy labelled records, not hand-entered summaries. diagnostics.json contains oracle, leakage, covariance, reset, near-unit-root, informative-missingness-warning, and deterministic-rerun checks. The single PNG is derived from the same frozen arrays and metrics.
The required execution in the bundled runtime is:
/Users/bytedance/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/python/bin/python3 toy-models/linear-gaussian-inference-ladder.py
By default the script generates the repository artifacts and verifies them, including a clean temporary regeneration and byte comparison. Explicit --generate and --verify modes are also available. JSON serialization order, float formatting, CSV row order, and PNG output are fixed so determinism is testable. No external data, network access, system package, or private resource is used at execution time.



The following external evidence was actually retrieved and inspected for this design; repository Method summaries were used only as terminology anchors.

Kalman (1960): 12-page article PDF, bibliographic metadata and article-level text inspected. Equation-level inspection covered the “Optimal Estimates” distinction among smoothing, filtering, and prediction; the state-space Problem I; the recursive innovation/projection construction and Theorem 3; covariance recursion; examples; and conclusion. The appendix was not inspected line by line. Kalman’s displayed observation formulation is historically broader/different in notation from the additive-noise scalar model used here, so Särkkä supplies the direct Bayesian additive-noise equations (Kalman 1960).
Rauch, Tung, and Striebel (1965): 14-page publisher-rendered PDF containing the six-page AIAA article plus appended citation material. Publication metadata, abstract, model/criterion setup, sections 3.1 and 3.2 at equation level, the numerical-example discussion, and section 5 conclusion were inspected. Appended citation lists and every continuous-time appendix equation were not inspected in detail (Rauch et al. 1965).
Särkkä (2013): author-hosted 252-page book PDF. Equation-level inspection covered sections 4.1–4.3 (state-space factorization, Bayesian filter, Kalman filter), 8.1–8.2 (fixed-interval Bayesian smoothing and RTS recursions), and 12.1–12.1.1 (unknown parameters and prediction-error/marginal-likelihood factorization). The full book was not read line by line (Särkkä 2013).

The inspected sources support the fixed-parameter filtering/smoothing targets, recursions, and likelihood factorization. They do not supply the particular seeds, finite grid, stress magnitudes, or acceptance tolerances; those are predeclared LDG design choices.



The scientific-design executor ran target structural and diff checks, the implementation owner ran deterministic script and artifact checks, and the parent orchestrator completed repository validation, tests, target/index/full-site renders, independent scientific and implementation focused review, and owner-authorized promotion under the recorded review decision. The executor did not review its own work.





Complete Toy Model schema at L1/stable with generated empirical results distinguished from model-derived expectations.
Generation, masking, parameter selection, inference, and scoring are separated.
Ground truth, primary parameters, splits, seeds, boundaries, and missing block are predeclared.
Known-parameter filtering, RTS smoothing, and direct batch conditioning have distinct information sets.
Prediction, latent recovery, model-conditional uncertainty, and parameter uncertainty are distinguished.
Finite-grid selection excludes test observations and all latent truth and is not called general ML estimation.
Correct-model, wrong-(q/r), missing-block, reset-boundary, near-unit-root, and informative-missingness conditions are bounded.
Online versus retrospective non-implication limits are explicit.
Artifact inventory, manifest fields, determinism, metrics schema, and numerical oracles match the backlog contract.
External evidence scope is recorded without claiming complete inspection.
Bounded implementation and artifacts generated and deterministically verified.
Independent scientific review PASS after focused re-review of the near-unit-root horizon diagnostic.
Independent implementation review PASS after focused re-review of seven bounded verification and consistency corrections.
Target and repository validation PASS, including deterministic regeneration, 51-object structural validation, 31 unit tests, target/index/full-site renders, and diff checks.
