title: Linear-Gaussian Inference Ladder
Linear-Gaussian Inference Ladder
text:
For each independent sequence, the retained scalar latent state is (z_{1:T}), the observed scalar is (x_{1:T}), and the complete-data generator is
\[
z_1\sim\mathcal N(0,p_1),
\qquad
p_1=\frac{q}{1-a^2},
\]
\[
z_{t+1}=a z_t+w_t,
\qquad
w_t\overset{\mathrm{iid}}\sim\mathcal N(0,q),
\]
\[
x_t=z_t+v_t,
\qquad
v_t\overset{\mathrm{iid}}\sim\mathcal N(0,r),
\]
with (z_1), all (w_t), and all (v_t) mutually independent. The primary parameters are fixed before simulation:
\[
a=0.85,
\qquad
q=0.10,
\qquad
r=0.40,
\qquad
p_1=\frac{0.10}{1-0.85^2}.
\]
The initialization is the stationary zero-mean law for this scalar stable model. Stationarity is a property of the declared generator and initialization, not a conclusion inferred from a finite simulated trace.
The observation map is the identity. This removes latent-coordinate ambiguity for this bounded scalar recovery test, but it does not make the latent state directly observed: (x_t) still contains independent measurement noise. Retaining (z_t) for scoring is a simulation privilege. Test latent truth is never an input to parameter selection, filtering, smoothing, or batch conditioning.

Assign immutable sequence boundaries. Train, validation, and test sequences are independent replicates. Every recovery method starts each sequence from the declared prior; no posterior mean or covariance crosses a true boundary.
Create masks without changing the complete arrays. The primary complete-data mask retains every observation. The missing-block mask removes a predeclared contiguous interval only on test copies. The informative-missingness negative control derives a separate observation-magnitude-dependent mask from the frozen test observations and is never treated as ignorable evidence.
Select parameters without latent truth. The finite grid reads only train and validation observations, masks, and sequence boundaries. It may use innovation likelihood, but no latent state or test quantity.
Run recovery. Known-parameter and selected-parameter methods receive observations, masks, boundaries, and their declared parameter tuple.
Score last. Latent truth is joined only after all posterior and predictive outputs have been frozen.

This ordering prevents generation from being mistaken for recovery and prevents test latent states from becoming pseudo-observations.

title: Linear-Gaussian Inference Ladder
text:
The implementation must use the existing Python/NumPy runtime and must not install a dependency. For each split, generation is vectorized across independent sequences only where this does not obscure resets. Stored arrays preserve a sequence axis; flattening sequences before inference is prohibited except in the explicit reset-boundary negative control.
The generator retains (z) and (x) with split and sequence identities. Recovery functions receive observations, masks, boundaries, and parameters rather than the latent array. Computed poison diagnostics change test observations or every latent array and verify that grid selection and recovery outputs remain unchanged; separate-sequence invocation is also compared numerically with the stacked multi-sequence path. Retained latent values enter only the later scoring functions.


Let
\[
\mathcal I_t^{\mathrm{F}}=\sigma(x_s:\ s\le t,\ x_s\text{ observed})
\]
be the online information set. Before observing (x_t), the scalar prediction is
\[
m_{t\mid t-1}=a m_{t-1\mid t-1},
\qquad
p_{t\mid t-1}=a^2p_{t-1\mid t-1}+q,
\]
with (m_{1}=0) and (p_{1}=p_1). For an observed (x_t),
\[
\nu_t=x_t-m_{t\mid t-1},
\qquad
s_t=p_{t\mid t-1}+r,
\qquad
k_t=\frac{p_{t\mid t-1}}{s_t},
\]
\[
m_{t\mid t}=m_{t\mid t-1}+k_t\nu_t,
\qquad
p_{t\mid t}=p_{t\mid t-1}-k_t^2s_t.
\]
These are the scalar specialization of exact linear-Gaussian Bayesian filtering (Kalman 1960; Särkkä 2013, theorem 4.2). If (x_t) is missing, no pseudo-observation is inserted:
\[
m_{t\mid t}=m_{t\mid t-1},
\qquad
p_{t\mid t}=p_{t\mid t-1}.
\]
Thus a filter traverses the declared missing block by repeated open-loop prediction. It cannot use observations after the current time.



Let
\[
\mathcal I_T^{\mathrm{S}}=\sigma(x_s:\ 1\le s\le T,\ x_s\text{ observed})
\]
be the retrospective information set. Starting from (m_{TT},p_{TT}), the scalar RTS recursion is
\[
j_t=\frac{p_{t\mid t}a}{p_{t+1\mid t}},
\]
\[
m_{t\mid T}=m_{t\mid t}+j_t\left(m_{t+1\mid T}-m_{t+1\mid t}\right),
\]
\[
p_{t\mid T}=p_{t\mid t}+j_t^2\left(p_{t+1\mid T}-p_{t+1\mid t}\right).
\]
Rauch, Tung, and Striebel derive the backward recursion from the forward filtering solution; the modern Bayesian statement makes explicit that it computes (p(z_tx_{1:T})), whereas filtering computes (p(z_tx_{1:t})) (Rauch et al. 1965, sec. 3.2; Särkkä 2013, secs. 8.1–8.2). Later observations may therefore revise states inside the missing block. That revision is valid only retrospectively and must never be described as information available online at time (t).



For a bounded sequence, construct the prior path mean (m_z=0) and covariance (K_z) from the declared prior and transition recursion. Under the stationary primary model,
\[
(K_z)_{ij}=p_1 a^{|i-j|}.
\]
For observed time indices (O), let (H_O) select those state coordinates and let (x_O) be the corresponding observation vector. Direct conditioning gives
\[
\mu_{z\mid x_O}
=m_z+K_zH_O^\top
\left(H_OK_zH_O^\top+rI\right)^{-1}
(x_O-H_Om_z),
\]
\[
\Sigma_{z\mid x_O}
=K_z-K_zH_O^\top
\left(H_OK_zH_O^\top+rI\right)^{-1}
H_OK_z.
\]
The implementation must use a linear solve, not an explicit matrix inverse. For each short oracle sequence, conditioning on observations through (t) supplies the current-time filter oracle, while conditioning on every observed time through (T) supplies the full smoother oracle. Agreement with this independently assembled joint Gaussian is an implementation test, not an additional estimator (Särkkä 2013, secs. 4.1–4.3, 8.1–8.2).

title: Linear-Gaussian Inference Ladder
Linear-Gaussian Inference Ladder
text:
These are model-derived expectations, not prefilled empirical results.

In exact arithmetic under the correct fixed model, recursive filtering and smoothing should equal direct Gaussian conditioning for the same observations and information set (Särkkä 2013, theorems 4.2 and 8.2).
Under the exact fixed model, (p_{tT}p_{tt}) because smoothing conditions on a superset of observations. Floating-point violations beyond tolerance indicate an implementation problem, not negative variance.
Under the correct generator, posterior means are conditional-MSE-optimal for their own information sets. Across repeated draws, the smoother can have lower expected latent MSE than the filter, but any finite test realization may deviate. Lower smoothing RMSE does not make smoothing suitable for an online task.
During a missing block, the filter mean and variance evolve only through the transition. The smoother may revise that interval using later observations, but only after the interval endpoint is available.
Wrong (q/r) changes gains, innovation variance, posterior width, and retrospective coupling. The direction and size of finite-sample metric changes are empirical outputs, not guaranteed numerical values.
Near (a=1), stationary variance and long-horizon predictive uncertainty are larger and initialization effects can persist. This stress is reported separately rather than used to redefine primary success.

title: Linear-Gaussian Inference Ladder
text:
Use the true tuple for filtering, smoothing, prediction, and batch conditioning. This condition tests exact-inference implementation and finite-sample recovery separately:

batch-versus-recursion discrepancies test numerical implementation;
latent RMSE and coverage test recovery under one realized sample from the declared correct model; and
predictive negative log likelihood and innovations test the observation distribution.

Low RMSE is not required for posterior correctness on every realization, because process and observation noise leave irreducible uncertainty.



Apply q_small_r_large and q_large_r_small to the unchanged primary test observations. Score predictive likelihood, filter and smoother latent RMSE, interval coverage, mean posterior variance, standardized innovation variance, and lag-1 autocorrelation. These are plug-in, misspecified posteriors. Their intervals do not become valid uncertainty statements about the true generator merely because the covariance recursion remains algebraically valid.



Remove zero-based observations (x_{30:45}) from every primary test sequence before both forward and backward inference. Score missing-block and observed-region errors separately. Innovation likelihood is computed only where observations are available. The filter’s block trajectory is an online prediction from pre-block information; the smoother’s block trajectory is a retrospective reconstruction using both sides. Comparing their RMSE must preserve that information-set difference.



Take the first two independently generated primary test sequences and, only for this negative control, concatenate them without resetting the prior at the join. Run the same parameter tuple as though the join were a real transition. Compare against correct separate-sequence inference using the inherited boundary prediction, first-state estimate difference, artificial-continuity magnitude, and proper-versus-joined RMSE over the first eight states of the second sequence.
The intended demonstration is that carrying a posterior across an independent reset can impose artificial continuity or otherwise distort inference near the join. The realized direction and magnitude are reported, not guaranteed. The negative control must never alter ordinary split handling.



Generate the separate (a=0.99) condition and compare matched-stationary versus tight-variance initialization. Report stationary prior variance, maximum filter and smoother variance, first-20-step mean/variance sensitivity, and covariance finiteness/nonnegativity. In addition, propagate variance without observations to fixed horizons (h{1,10,50,100,200}) under both initializations. This diagnostic separates long-horizon predictive uncertainty from posterior variance under continuous measurement updates. It is not a second primary model and cannot rescue a failed primary oracle.



For a warning-only negative control, hide an observation whenever (|x_t|>0.9). The ordinary skipped-update filter and smoother deliberately ignore the information carried by that observation-dependent mask. The posterior target under a joint observation–missingness model is therefore not the same as conditioning only on retained values. The resulting missing fraction, latent magnitude inside/outside the mask, and skipped-update filter RMSE are labeled uncorrected informative-missingness stress, excluded from primary acceptance, and used only to show why an ignorable-missingness interpretation fails. No correction or calibrated uncertainty claim is permitted without explicitly modeling the missingness process.

title: Linear-Gaussian Inference Ladder
text:
The implementation and generated diagnostics must assert all of the following.

Filter batch equivalence: for every short oracle prefix and observed mask, the recursive (m_{tt},p_{tt}) equal the current-time marginal from direct conditioning on observations through (t).
Smoother batch equivalence: all short-sequence (m_{tT},p_{tT}) equal the corresponding full batch posterior marginals.
Nested-information variance: (p_{tT}p_{tt}+10^{-12}) for the regular correct-model computations.
No look-ahead: changing (x_{t+1:T}) while holding (x_{1:t}) fixed cannot change any stored filter output through (t); it may change smoother outputs.
No latent leakage: parameter selection and inference inputs contain no latent array, and test latent truth is joined only by the scoring stage.
Boundary reset: separate-sequence outputs equal outputs obtained by running each sequence independently; only the named negative control omits the reset.
Numerical covariance: assembled batch covariances are symmetric within (10^{-12}); all scalar variances are at least (-10^{-12}); oracle mean and variance discrepancies are at most (10^{-10}) in absolute value.
Missing-block handling: no innovation or likelihood contribution is emitted at hidden times, and skipped updates equal predictions exactly within floating-point tolerance.
Determinism: two clean executions with the same runtime and command produce byte-identical manifest.json, metrics.csv, diagnostics.json, and summary.png.
Metric provenance: every metrics row identifies split, condition, parameter source, method, inference target, region, metric, and value.

Tolerance values belong in the manifest. Passing structural checks does not establish scientific model adequacy.

title: Linear-Gaussian Inference Ladder
text:
Filter reads the future: any dependence of a filter output at (t) on (x_{t+1:T}) is leakage and a hard failure.
Smoother mislabeled online: a retrospective estimate presented as available at time (t) is an inferential failure even if its arithmetic is correct.
Batch disagreement: discrepancies above tolerance under the same fixed model indicate indexing, covariance, masking, or conditioning errors.
Latent truth enters selection: any grid criterion, preprocessing decision, or posterior conditioned on (z_t) invalidates the learned-parameter comparison.
State propagates across true boundaries: failure to reset invents dependence between independent sequences.
Wrong-noise certainty interpreted as calibrated: covariance is conditional on the assumed tuple; misspecified plug-in intervals can be narrow and wrong.
Parameter uncertainty omitted silently: selected-grid posterior intervals exclude uncertainty over the selection procedure and candidate tuple.
Missingness treated as ignorable without justification: state-dependent absence changes the conditioning problem.
Near-unit-root results pooled with primary results: doing so changes the acceptance population and obscures initialization sensitivity.
Plausible figure replaces numerical checks: visual smoothness cannot verify a posterior, a boundary, or calibration.
Recovery treated as mechanism: successful state estimation in a simulator does not establish a causal or biological transition law.

title: Linear-Gaussian Inference Ladder
text:
The recovery outputs are kept distinct.


For observed times, the one-step observation predictive law is
\[
x_t\mid x_{1:t-1}\sim
\mathcal N(m_{t\mid t-1},s_t),
\qquad
s_t=p_{t\mid t-1}+r.
\]
The held-out one-step negative log likelihood and standardized innovation (_t/) score this observation prediction. Smoothing does not produce a new prospective sequence likelihood; the same forward predictive factorization supplies the fixed-parameter likelihood (Särkkä 2013, sec. 12.1.1).



Filter and smoother posterior means are scored against retained (z_t) only after inference. Filtering RMSE evaluates online recovery; smoothing RMSE evaluates retrospective recovery. They are different tasks because their conditioning sigma-fields differ.



Pointwise 95% coverage uses
\[
m\pm 1.959963984540054\sqrt{p}
\]
for the relevant filter or smoother posterior. Coverage is aggregated across independent test sequences and time points, with missing-block inside/outside records. It describes repeated-simulation behavior under a fixed assumed tuple. A single interval does not carry a frequentist guarantee for one state, and finite-sample aggregate coverage need not equal 0.95 exactly.



Known-parameter intervals condition on the true tuple. Selected-grid intervals condition on one frozen selected tuple. Neither integrates over parameter uncertainty. The learned-versus-known gap is reported in prediction, recovery, and coverage metrics, but no plug-in covariance is called total uncertainty.

title: Linear-Gaussian Inference Ladder
text:
Stationary-mean reference. Use the generator’s zero stationary mean as a deliberately non-temporal latent point reference. No latent posterior coverage is reported.
Persistence / last observation. Use a latent point proxy equal to the most recent observed (x); before any observation use zero. It has no model-conditional state interval.
Open-loop state prediction. Assimilate the first available observation once using the declared model, then propagate without further updates. It is a bounded no-reassimilation baseline; prediction-only propagation inside a missing block is also the filter’s exact behavior conditional on its last filtered state.
Known-parameter Kalman filter. Compute online predictive and filtering distributions using only data through the current time (Kalman 1960; Särkkä 2013, ch. 4).
Known-parameter RTS smoother. Run the fixed-interval backward pass after the complete declared interval is available (Rauch et al. 1965; Särkkä 2013, ch. 8).
Direct batch Gaussian conditioning. Use only bounded short sequences as an independently assembled correctness oracle.
Selected-grid filter and smoother. Freeze the finite-grid tuple selected by train/validation innovation likelihood, then evaluate on untouched test sequences.

Static Factor Analysis is a conceptual prerequisite and order-blind comparison, not an executable candidate in this scalar unit. It cannot represent the transition or distinguish online from retrospective information merely because factor scores happen to be smooth.

title: Linear-Gaussian Inference Ladder
text:
The passed correct-model oracle establishes that, for the declared scalar LGSSM and numerical tolerance, the implementation returns the same fixed-parameter Gaussian marginals by recursive and batch routes. Recovery metrics would then describe finite simulations from that generator. They would not establish that any real data source is linear, Gaussian, stationary, first-order Markov, correctly segmented, or governed by the recovered transition.
Filtering and smoothing must remain separate in every table and caption. The filter answers an online question with (x_{1:t}); the smoother answers a retrospective question with (x_{1:T}). More information can improve retrospective state reconstruction without making the smoother a fair competitor for a prospective decision.
Wrong-(q/r), missing-block, boundary, and near-unit-root conditions diagnose sensitivity to assumptions. They do not provide a generic ranking of all state-space methods. A selected grid point is one data-dependent plug-in model among 27 candidates, not recovered ground truth.

title: Linear-Gaussian Inference Ladder
text:
It does not prove that observed data lie on a manifold or possess non-Euclidean geometry.
It does not identify a causal, physical, neural, or biological state.
It does not show that temporal correlation is a mechanistic dynamical law.
It does not turn decoding or latent RMSE into evidence of representation.
It does not prove unrestricted parameter identifiability or successful maximum-likelihood learning.
It does not include parameter uncertainty in plug-in posterior intervals.
It does not make fixed-interval smoothing online, causal, or prospectively available.
It does not validate skipped updates under informative missingness.
It does not imply that low reconstruction error, nominal coverage, or a smooth plot is sufficient evidence for model adequacy.
It does not authorize extension to another Phase 3 candidate or promotion to stable.

title: Linear-Gaussian Inference Ladder
text: Before a real-data use, the analyst would need to justify observation units, sampling intervals, sequence resets, covariates, latent dimension, transition and noise structure, missingness, nonstationarity, and evaluation splits. Parameters and preprocessing must be learned on independent training units. Prospective tasks require filtering or forecasting; retrospective smoothing outputs cannot be backdated into an online analysis. Residual and predictive checks should test Gaussianity, white innovations, heteroscedasticity, regime changes, and boundary effects. None of those extensions is executed here.

The following external evidence was actually retrieved and inspected for this design; repository Method summaries were used only as terminology anchors.

Kalman (1960): 12-page article PDF, bibliographic metadata and article-level text inspected. Equation-level inspection covered the “Optimal Estimates” distinction among smoothing, filtering, and prediction; the state-space Problem I; the recursive innovation/projection construction and Theorem 3; covariance recursion; examples; and conclusion. The appendix was not inspected line by line. Kalman’s displayed observation formulation is historically broader/different in notation from the additive-noise scalar model used here, so Särkkä supplies the direct Bayesian additive-noise equations (Kalman 1960).

Appended citation lists and every continuous-time appendix equation were not inspected in detail (Rauch et al. 1965).
Särkkä (2013): author-hosted 252-page book PDF. Equation-level inspection covered sections 4.1–4.3 (state-space factorization, Bayesian filter, Kalman filter), 8.1–8.2 (fixed-interval Bayesian smoothing and RTS recursions), and 12.1–12.1.1 (unknown parameters and prediction-error/marginal-likelihood factorization). The full book was not read line by line (Särkkä 2013).

title: Static Linear Latent Recovery
text:
This L1/stable Toy Model is the Candidate A generation/recovery slice. It asks whether PCA and Gaussian latent-factor models recover the distinct targets their criteria define, and how residual misspecification, weak uniquenesses, nuisance variance, outliers, and preprocessing leakage make those targets diverge. Numerical values below are deterministic outputs under master seed 20260819; they are not population theorems or real-data claims.
Assumed background: centered covariance PCA, Gaussian likelihood, linear subspaces, principal angles, and the Gaussian factor model. The stable Method Objects provide LDG terminology but do not replace the external evidence inspection recorded below.


For observations generated by a known rank-two Gaussian factor model:

does ordinary PCA recover the leading eigenspace of the observable covariance;
does correctly specified diagonal-noise FA recover the common loading subspace, common covariance, diagonal uniquenesses, and observable covariance up to loading rotations;
how does isotropic-noise PPCA differ from heterogeneous-noise FA; and
how do repeated signal eigenvalues, near-zero uniquenesses, correlated residuals, high nuisance variance, outliers, and pooled train/test scaling expose criterion or evaluation failures?

The object keeps four targets distinct:

loading subspace \(\mathcal S_\Lambda=\operatorname{col}(\Lambda)\);
common covariance \(\Lambda\Lambda^\top\);
observable covariance \(C=\Lambda\Lambda^\top+\Sigma_\epsilon\); and
the rank-two population principal subspace of \(C\).

PCA is scored against the last target. Diagonal FA is scored against the loading/common-covariance target only where its diagonal residual model is correctly specified and the displayed loading matrix passes the sufficient rank diagnostic stated below. Heterogeneous uniqueness means these subspaces need not coincide (Jolliffe and Cadima 2016; Anderson and Rubin 1956; Tipping and Bishop 1999).



The ambient dimension is \(p=8\) and latent rank is \(q=2\). For each independent row,
\[
z_i\sim\mathcal N(0,I_2),\qquad
\epsilon_i\sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_\epsilon),\qquad
x_i=\Lambda z_i+\epsilon_i.
\]
The latent draws and residuals are mutually independent. The base loading basis \(U\) is the deterministic QR-orthonormalization of
\[
B=\begin{pmatrix}
1.0&0.2\\
0.7&-0.5\\
0.4&1.0\\
-0.6&0.8\\
0.9&0.3\\
-0.2&-0.9\\
0.5&-0.4\\
-0.7&-0.2
\end{pmatrix},
\]
with QR signs chosen so the diagonal of \(R\) is nonnegative. The primary loading is
\[
\Lambda=U\operatorname{diag}(2.0,1.25),
\]
and the primary uniqueness vector is
\[
\psi=(0.12,0.20,0.32,0.48,0.70,0.95,1.25,1.60).
\]
The retained truth contains \(z\), \(\Lambda\), \(\Sigma_\epsilon\), \(C\), the loading subspace, and the population principal subspace. Latent arrays enter only scoring and poison tests; fitting and model selection receive observations only.


Correct diagonal residual specification alone is not an identification result. For each displayed loading matrix, the implementation checks the following Anderson–Rubin-style sufficient rank condition: after deleting any one of the eight rows, the remaining rows contain two disjoint two-row submatrices, each of rank two. Specialized adaptations were not inspected exhaustively (Jolliffe and Cadima 2016).
Anderson and Rubin (1956): the 40-page proceedings PDF was inspected at equation level for the Gaussian factor model, covariance decomposition, loading rotation, identification conditions, likelihood, diagonal-uniqueness iteration, isotropic-noise/PCA connection, and measurement-unit discussion. Part II proofs and all testing/asymptotic sections were not read line by line (Anderson and Rubin 1956).

Applied examples and Appendix B were inspected only at overview level (Tipping and Bishop 1999).

These sources do not supply the simulator dimensions, seeds, stress magnitudes, optimizer budget, or numerical tolerances; those are LDG design choices.

title: Research Questions
text: Research Question Objects connect established knowledge to falsifiable methodological questions. Items published here are explicitly exploratory rather than established claims.

title: Demixing and Rotational Projection Robustness Benchmark
text:
P4-U04 asks two separate synthetic questions.

Label-dependent demixing: under known stimulus- and decision-dependent linear effects, when do condition means, PCA, marginal PCA, bounded dPCA and ridge decoding recover their own declared held-out targets, and how do those targets respond to collinearity, cell imbalance, label permutation, pseudo-populations, trial averaging and sample size?
Rotational projection: under known rotational and non-rotational trajectory families, when do PCA planes, unrestricted derivative regression, skew-constrained jPCA-like fitting, symmetric fitting, input-aware fitting and fixed/random/control planes recover held-out derivative, plane, angular-rate, tangential-motion or covariance-control targets?

The two tasks have separate generators, scenario grids, methods, applicability rules, metrics, summaries and figure panels. No cross-task normalization, aggregate score, rank or winner is computed. Marginal reconstruction, label decoding, marginal-subspace recovery, rotational-plane recovery, angular-rate recovery and derivative prediction are also never combined into one score.





The demixing generator has eight observed features, 12 aligned time bins and a balanced binary stimulus \(s\in\{-1,1\}\) and decision \(d\in\{-1,1\}\) design in the reference scenario. A trial has clean signal
\[
y_{s,d}(t)
= \mu(t)
+0.9\,s\,f_s(t)v_s
+0.75\,d\,f_d(t)v_d,
\]
plus independent Gaussian observation noise with standard deviation \(0.42\). The reference \(v_s\) and \(v_d\) are orthonormal. The near-collinear scenario replaces the second direction by a normalized perturbation of the first. There is no interaction effect in this bounded generator. Trial shifts, feature-wise trial reassignment and label permutations are scenario operations, not hidden changes to the reference target.
The known targets are the stimulus and decision condition-mean marginalizations and their generating one-dimensional feature directions. Labels are observed supervision for fitting; clean signals and generating directions are unavailable to fitting and enter only scoring or verification.



The rotational generator has four latent coordinates, eight observed features, six conditions, 31 physical-time samples on \([0,1.2]\), and independent trials. The reference latent matrix contains a rate-four planar rotation and a second, slower damped rotational block. The primary plane/rate target is the first known observed-space plane and angular rate \(4\). Other scenarios replace the latent family with symmetric decay, latency sequences or input-driven trajectories, or alter the observation metric and preprocessing.
The observation map is an eight-by-four orthonormal embedding in ordinary scenarios and a declared nonorthogonal embedding in the metric stress. Gaussian latent and observation perturbations are added independently. Known latent states, embedding and generating matrices are scoring/verification truth only. They are not supplied to fitted projections.




Generation is task-specific and precedes all fitting.

Demixing: each scenario-replicate independently generates train, validation and test trials. Reference per-cell counts are 20/10/12, giving actual split totals 80/40/48. The small-sample per-cell counts 5/4/12 give totals 20/16/48; large-sample counts 45/18/18 give totals 180/72/72. The missing-cell training matrix is [[20,20],[20,0]], for total 60 and design rank three; validation/test remain balanced with totals 40/48. The unbalanced training matrix is [[40,5],[6,20]], for total 71 and design rank four; its validation/test totals are 40/48.
Rotation: each scenario-replicate independently generates 7/4/5 trials per condition for train/validation/test. Across six conditions, the actual totals are 42/24/30. Condition trajectories share the declared scenario family but receive independent perturbations.

Demixing condition means are arithmetic means within each observed cell. The complete-design marginalization then gives the four cells equal weight rather than weighting them by trial count. Rotational preprocessing first averages trials within each condition; when subtraction is enabled, it subtracts the across-condition mean separately at each time point.
The executable is benchmark-local. It records SHA-256 digests of the stable Phase 3 demixing and rotational-control executables as scientific-design provenance, but it does not claim to call or executable-reuse their numerical routines.

The grid is core-plus-stress, not a factorial isolation of individual causes. The missing-cell training design has rank three rather than the required rank four. The benchmark therefore reports the design-rank diagnostic and retains held-out decoder scores, but labels every otherwise applicable balanced marginal-reconstruction and marginal-subspace row invalid with reason incomplete_factorial_design_rank_3_of_4. It does not use grand-mean filling to claim identified balanced marginal recovery.

Plane and angular-rate truth are reported only for declared rotational scenarios and are omitted for decay, latency, input and covariance-control families where that target is not defined.




Demixing controls include permuted labels, incomplete and unequal cells, within-cell pseudo-population reassignment and non-wrapping trial-alignment mismatch. The shuffled-dPCA control independently permutes both training and validation labels, reselects its own dPCA ridge parameter on the shuffled validation target, and then refits. Each shuffled decoder likewise independently reselects its own ridge parameter from shuffled training/validation labels. Thus shuffled controls do not inherit the lawful method’s selected parameter. A label permutation is expected to change supervised fitted states; it is not another independent replicate.
The pseudo-population operation permutes each feature’s complete trajectory only among trials in the same split and condition cell. Labels and cell means are preserved to numerical precision across all replicates (maximum discrepancy \(3.33\times10^{-16}\)). Across the three replicates, the off-diagonal trial-noise covariance change ranges from 0.0523–0.0644 in train, 0.0685–0.0766 in validation and 0.0690–0.0772 in test. It therefore isolates loss of simultaneous within-cell trial covariance rather than destroying condition means.
Rotational controls include symmetric dynamics, latency sequences, common input, short arcs, non-wrapping timing jitter, smoothing and subtraction alternatives, nonorthogonal metric distortion, a deterministic seed-derived random plane and a selected covariance control. The latter attempts 24 predeclared seed-derived proposals, each applying a cyclic condition shift separately to every PCA coordinate. A proposal is admissible only when at least two coordinate shifts are distinct and it materially changes cross-coordinate condition correspondence; a uniform all-coordinate shift is excluded as a global relabeling/no-op. Selection maximizes training covariance cosine similarity among admissible proposals only, with match threshold 0.97. Replicates 0/1/2 have 23/24/24 admissible proposals and select proposals 0/19/4 with similarities 0.999995, 0.999990 and 0.999985. All selected controls use multiple distinct shifts, materially alter cross-coordinate correspondence, and are labelled matched. Selection and matching occur on training scores; the control does not preserve condition pairing or establish dynamics.
No stress case is discarded because it weakens the preferred method, and no post-hoc scenario-specific parameter search is performed.



Each of the 19 scenarios has three independent replicates. PCG64 seeds are deterministically derived from master seed 20260820, task, stable scenario hash, replicate, stage, split and, where needed, trial/control index. Methods within a replicate share the same generated data for paired comparison.
The q10, median and q90 summaries therefore use three replicate-level values. They are descriptive finite-sample summaries, not confidence intervals or stable tail estimates. Trials, conditions, cells and time points are not promoted to independent replicates.



Generation, fitting/selection, frozen recovery and scoring are separate stages.

Demixing fitting accepts only train/validation observations and labels. dPCA regularization and ridge-decoder regularization are selected without test data. Frozen recovery accepts fitted states and test observations/labels; truth is joined only in scoring.
Rotational preprocessing, PCA and derivative models are fitted from training observations and known training inputs where declared. Frozen recovery accepts fitted states, test observations and test inputs. Test latent states and the true embedding remain scoring-only.
Excluded test observations and truth cannot enter fitting by function signature. Poison diagnostics report zero fitted-state discrepancy for test exclusion and zero fixed-observation recovery discrepancy for truth poison.
Complete trials remain within one split. Adjacent time bins are never split across train and test.

The label- and condition-permutation controls are explicit alternate fitting paths, not leakage into the lawful path.

The unrestricted, skew, symmetric and input-aware models share the same training PCA coordinate system. Their derivative predictions are evaluated on held-out central finite differences. pca_plane is coordinates [0,1], whereas fixed_plane is the deliberately distinct coordinates [0,2]; they are not aliases. The verifier’s maximum projector difference is 1.0, and their clean plane-angle medians are 0.5389° and 89.6500°, respectively. A retrospective condition-mean projection is not an online state estimator, and no online claim is made.




For selected_dpca, the ridge grid is
\[
\lambda\in\{10^{-4},10^{-2},10^{-1},1\}.
\]
Each candidate is fitted on training condition means and scored by the sum of validation stimulus- and decision-marginal mean-squared errors; ties use the smaller ordered \(\lambda\). Each ridge decoder uses the same grid with validation classification error and the same deterministic tie rule. The lawful and shuffled dPCA/decoder paths each perform their own selection on their own labels before their states are frozen. In the reference replicate used by the verifier, lawful/shuffled dPCA both select 1.0; lawful stimulus/decision decoders select \(10^{-4}/10^{-4}\), while shuffled decoders select \(10^{-4}/1.0\). These values are diagnostics for that replicate, not universal hyperparameters.
Rotational methods have no fitted hyperparameter search in this bounded implementation. Window, smoothing, subtraction, fixed/random planes and condition permutation are predeclared scenario or method choices, not selected from test performance.



Demixing recovery rebuilds held-out condition means and marginalizations from complete test trials. Training condition means, global/marginal PCA projectors, selected dPCA maps and shuffled-control maps are then applied according to their fixed roles. Trial decoders use three predeclared temporal averages per feature. The clean trial signal and generating directions are never inputs to recovery.
Rotational recovery applies training-fitted smoothing/subtraction statistics, feature mean and rank-four PCA basis to held-out condition means. Central finite differences define held-out derivative targets. Fitted derivative maps predict in the frozen PCA coordinate system. Plane methods project those same held-out scores. The input-aware model alone receives the declared held-out input sequence.



Every results.csv row has task, scenario, replicate, seed, metric-specific provenance/split/evaluation stage, method family, information set, parameter source, target, status/reason, per-cell count arrays and actual split totals. Where relevant it also records selected hyperparameter, design rank, covariance-control match status and proposal index. The artifact contains only the following metrics.

Derivative RMSE, plane angle, angular-rate error and tangential ratio are not interchangeable evidence. In particular, tangential motion in a selected plane can occur for transients or input-driven sequences.
Each metric is first aggregated across its declared held-out cells/trials, conditions or derivative pairs into one scenario-replicate-method value. diagnostics.json then reports q10, median, q90, applicability rate and failure rate across the three replicates for each task \(\times\) scenario \(\times\) method \(\times\) metric group.




The full Cartesian task-specific inventories are retained:

Applicability is resolved before numerical failure. Every row has one status:

ok: applicable and finite;
nonconvergence: linear-algebra failure in an applicable path;
invalid: malformed, missing or non-finite applicable score;
inapplicable: the method/scenario does not define the metric target.

Natural execution produced 1,041 ok, 1,617 inapplicable, 54 invalid and zero nonconvergence rows. By task, demixing has 567 ok, 891 inapplicable and 54 invalid; rotation has 474 ok and 726 inapplicable. All 54 natural invalid rows are the three missing-cell replicates’ otherwise applicable balanced marginal reconstruction/subspace combinations; the design rank is three of four. Every non-ok row has a machine-readable reason and no value. The absence of natural nonconvergence is not a robustness claim: real-path fault injection verifies both invalid and nonconvergence, while preserving inapplicable precedence.
Examples of inapplicability are decoder methods on marginal reconstruction, reconstruction methods on decoding, symmetric/input-aware fits on plane or rate targets, and plane/rate truth in non-rotational scenarios.

Separate demixing and rotational task summaries


The upper panels show only reference stimulus marginal NMSE and reference stimulus decoding. The lower panels show only clean held-out derivative RMSE and clean rotational-plane angle. pca_plane and fixed_plane are visibly and numerically distinct. No panel mixes the two tasks or treats one target as a proxy for another.




This object establishes only behavior under the declared generators, splits, scenario grids, targets, metrics and fitted information sets.

Demixing is label- and loss-dependent. It does not establish statistical independence, blind-source separation, unique latent causes, neural modules, anatomy, mechanism or causality.
Decoding accuracy is not representation, marginal reconstruction or demixing. A shuffled-label control is a supervision control, not a causal intervention on the data-generating system.
Missing/unbalanced cells and pseudo-populations change the estimand and available joint information. Finite output does not restore unidentified factorial effects or simultaneous noise structure.
Trial averaging and aligned smooth condition means can hide trial-level variability. They are not evidence for latent dynamics.
A rotational projection is not an oscillator, autonomous dynamical system, vector field or mechanism. Skew-constrained derivative fit describes a projection under declared preprocessing and metric.
A good plane angle does not imply good derivative prediction; high tangential ratio does not imply a true rotational generator; good derivative prediction does not imply autonomy or causality.
Latency sequences, common input, smoothing, subtraction, short windows, timing jitter and nonorthogonal coordinates can create, remove or distort rotational summaries.
No result establishes manifold structure, intrinsic dimension, biological validity, real-data transfer or universal method superiority.

title: Demixing and Rotational Projection Robustness Benchmark
text:
P4-U04 asks two separate synthetic questions.

Label-dependent demixing: under known stimulus- and decision-dependent linear effects, when do condition means, PCA, marginal PCA, bounded dPCA and ridge decoding recover their own declared held-out targets, and how do those targets respond to collinearity, cell imbalance, label permutation, pseudo-populations, trial averaging and sample size?
Rotational projection: under known rotational and non-rotational trajectory families, when do PCA planes, unrestricted derivative regression, skew-constrained jPCA-like fitting, symmetric fitting, input-aware fitting and fixed/random/control planes recover held-out derivative, plane, angular-rate, tangential-motion or covariance-control targets?

The two tasks have separate generators, scenario grids, methods, applicability rules, metrics, summaries and figure panels. No cross-task normalization, aggregate score, rank or winner is computed. Marginal reconstruction, label decoding, marginal-subspace recovery, rotational-plane recovery, angular-rate recovery and derivative prediction are also never combined into one score.

title: Demixing and Rotational Projection Robustness Benchmark
text:
The demixing generator has eight observed features, 12 aligned time bins and a balanced binary stimulus \(s\in\{-1,1\}\) and decision \(d\in\{-1,1\}\) design in the reference scenario. A trial has clean signal
\[
y_{s,d}(t)
= \mu(t)
+0.9\,s\,f_s(t)v_s
+0.75\,d\,f_d(t)v_d,
\]
plus independent Gaussian observation noise with standard deviation \(0.42\). The reference \(v_s\) and \(v_d\) are orthonormal. The near-collinear scenario replaces the second direction by a normalized perturbation of the first. There is no interaction effect in this bounded generator. Trial shifts, feature-wise trial reassignment and label permutations are scenario operations, not hidden changes to the reference target.
The known targets are the stimulus and decision condition-mean marginalizations and their generating one-dimensional feature directions. Labels are observed supervision for fitting; clean signals and generating directions are unavailable to fitting and enter only scoring or verification.



The rotational generator has four latent coordinates, eight observed features, six conditions, 31 physical-time samples on \([0,1.2]\), and independent trials. The reference latent matrix contains a rate-four planar rotation and a second, slower damped rotational block. The primary plane/rate target is the first known observed-space plane and angular rate \(4\). Other scenarios replace the latent family with symmetric decay, latency sequences or input-driven trajectories, or alter the observation metric and preprocessing.
The observation map is an eight-by-four orthonormal embedding in ordinary scenarios and a declared nonorthogonal embedding in the metric stress. Gaussian latent and observation perturbations are added independently. Known latent states, embedding and generating matrices are scoring/verification truth only. They are not supplied to fitted projections.

title: Demixing and Rotational Projection Robustness Benchmark
text:
Generation is task-specific and precedes all fitting.

Demixing: each scenario-replicate independently generates train, validation and test trials. Reference per-cell counts are 20/10/12, giving actual split totals 80/40/48. The small-sample per-cell counts 5/4/12 give totals 20/16/48; large-sample counts 45/18/18 give totals 180/72/72. The missing-cell training matrix is [[20,20],[20,0]], for total 60 and design rank three; validation/test remain balanced with totals 40/48. The unbalanced training matrix is [[40,5],[6,20]], for total 71 and design rank four; its validation/test totals are 40/48.
Rotation: each scenario-replicate independently generates 7/4/5 trials per condition for train/validation/test. Across six conditions, the actual totals are 42/24/30. Condition trajectories share the declared scenario family but receive independent perturbations.

Demixing condition means are arithmetic means within each observed cell. The complete-design marginalization then gives the four cells equal weight rather than weighting them by trial count. Rotational preprocessing first averages trials within each condition; when subtraction is enabled, it subtracts the across-condition mean separately at each time point.
The executable is benchmark-local. It records SHA-256 digests of the stable Phase 3 demixing and rotational-control executables as scientific-design provenance, but it does not claim to call or executable-reuse their numerical routines.

title: Demixing and Rotational Projection Robustness Benchmark
text:
Demixing controls include permuted labels, incomplete and unequal cells, within-cell pseudo-population reassignment and non-wrapping trial-alignment mismatch. The shuffled-dPCA control independently permutes both training and validation labels, reselects its own dPCA ridge parameter on the shuffled validation target, and then refits. Each shuffled decoder likewise independently reselects its own ridge parameter from shuffled training/validation labels. Thus shuffled controls do not inherit the lawful method’s selected parameter. A label permutation is expected to change supervised fitted states; it is not another independent replicate.
The pseudo-population operation permutes each feature’s complete trajectory only among trials in the same split and condition cell. Labels and cell means are preserved to numerical precision across all replicates (maximum discrepancy \(3.33\times10^{-16}\)). Across the three replicates, the off-diagonal trial-noise covariance change ranges from 0.0523–0.0644 in train, 0.0685–0.0766 in validation and 0.0690–0.0772 in test. It therefore isolates loss of simultaneous within-cell trial covariance rather than destroying condition means.
Rotational controls include symmetric dynamics, latency sequences, common input, short arcs, non-wrapping timing jitter, smoothing and subtraction alternatives, nonorthogonal metric distortion, a deterministic seed-derived random plane and a selected covariance control. The latter attempts 24 predeclared seed-derived proposals, each applying a cyclic condition shift separately to every PCA coordinate. A proposal is admissible only when at least two coordinate shifts are distinct and it materially changes cross-coordinate condition correspondence; a uniform all-coordinate shift is excluded as a global relabeling/no-op. Selection maximizes training covariance cosine similarity among admissible proposals only, with match threshold 0.97. Replicates 0/1/2 have 23/24/24 admissible proposals and select proposals 0/19/4 with similarities 0.999995, 0.999990 and 0.999985. All selected controls use multiple distinct shifts, materially alter cross-coordinate correspondence, and are labelled matched. Selection and matching occur on training scores; the control does not preserve condition pairing or establish dynamics.
No stress case is discarded because it weakens the preferred method, and no post-hoc scenario-specific parameter search is performed.

title: Demixing and Rotational Projection Robustness Benchmark
text:
Each of the 19 scenarios has three independent replicates. PCG64 seeds are deterministically derived from master seed 20260820, task, stable scenario hash, replicate, stage, split and, where needed, trial/control index. Methods within a replicate share the same generated data for paired comparison.
The q10, median and q90 summaries therefore use three replicate-level values. They are descriptive finite-sample summaries, not confidence intervals or stable tail estimates. Trials, conditions, cells and time points are not promoted to independent replicates.

title: Demixing and Rotational Projection Robustness Benchmark
text:
Generation, fitting/selection, frozen recovery and scoring are separate stages.

Demixing fitting accepts only train/validation observations and labels. dPCA regularization and ridge-decoder regularization are selected without test data. Frozen recovery accepts fitted states and test observations/labels; truth is joined only in scoring.
Rotational preprocessing, PCA and derivative models are fitted from training observations and known training inputs where declared. Frozen recovery accepts fitted states, test observations and test inputs. Test latent states and the true embedding remain scoring-only.
Excluded test observations and truth cannot enter fitting by function signature. Poison diagnostics report zero fitted-state discrepancy for test exclusion and zero fixed-observation recovery discrepancy for truth poison.
Complete trials remain within one split. Adjacent time bins are never split across train and test.

The label- and condition-permutation controls are explicit alternate fitting paths, not leakage into the lawful path.

title: Demixing and Rotational Projection Robustness Benchmark
text:
For selected_dpca, the ridge grid is
\[
\lambda\in\{10^{-4},10^{-2},10^{-1},1\}.
\]
Each candidate is fitted on training condition means and scored by the sum of validation stimulus- and decision-marginal mean-squared errors; ties use the smaller ordered \(\lambda\). Each ridge decoder uses the same grid with validation classification error and the same deterministic tie rule. The lawful and shuffled dPCA/decoder paths each perform their own selection on their own labels before their states are frozen. In the reference replicate used by the verifier, lawful/shuffled dPCA both select 1.0; lawful stimulus/decision decoders select \(10^{-4}/10^{-4}\), while shuffled decoders select \(10^{-4}/1.0\). These values are diagnostics for that replicate, not universal hyperparameters.
Rotational methods have no fitted hyperparameter search in this bounded implementation. Window, smoothing, subtraction, fixed/random planes and condition permutation are predeclared scenario or method choices, not selected from test performance.

title: Demixing and Rotational Projection Robustness Benchmark
text:
Demixing recovery rebuilds held-out condition means and marginalizations from complete test trials. Training condition means, global/marginal PCA projectors, selected dPCA maps and shuffled-control maps are then applied according to their fixed roles. Trial decoders use three predeclared temporal averages per feature. The clean trial signal and generating directions are never inputs to recovery.
Rotational recovery applies training-fitted smoothing/subtraction statistics, feature mean and rank-four PCA basis to held-out condition means. Central finite differences define held-out derivative targets. Fitted derivative maps predict in the frozen PCA coordinate system. Plane methods project those same held-out scores. The input-aware model alone receives the declared held-out input sequence.

title: Demixing and Rotational Projection Robustness Benchmark
text:
This object establishes only behavior under the declared generators, splits, scenario grids, targets, metrics and fitted information sets.

Demixing is label- and loss-dependent. It does not establish statistical independence, blind-source separation, unique latent causes, neural modules, anatomy, mechanism or causality.
Decoding accuracy is not representation, marginal reconstruction or demixing. A shuffled-label control is a supervision control, not a causal intervention on the data-generating system.
Missing/unbalanced cells and pseudo-populations change the estimand and available joint information. Finite output does not restore unidentified factorial effects or simultaneous noise structure.
Trial averaging and aligned smooth condition means can hide trial-level variability. They are not evidence for latent dynamics.
A rotational projection is not an oscillator, autonomous dynamical system, vector field or mechanism. Skew-constrained derivative fit describes a projection under declared preprocessing and metric.
A good plane angle does not imply good derivative prediction; high tangential ratio does not imply a true rotational generator; good derivative prediction does not imply autonomy or causality.
Latency sequences, common input, smoothing, subtraction, short windows, timing jitter and nonorthogonal coordinates can create, remove or distort rotational summaries.
No result establishes manifold structure, intrinsic dimension, biological validity, real-data transfer or universal method superiority.

title: Demixing and Rotational Projection Robustness Benchmark
Demixing and Rotational Projection Robustness Benchmark
text:
Independent scientific and implementation reviewers were read-only and independent of the executors. Their initial reviews returned REVISE on missing-cell design-rank invalidity, within-cell pseudo-populations, independent shuffled-control selection, non-wrapping shifts, split metadata, distinct plane references, and nontrivial covariance-matched proposals. The bounded correction pass addressed only those findings; focused scientific and implementation re-reviews both returned PASS with no unresolved finding.
The accepted validation record includes 61-object structural validation, 33 repository tests, the enhanced artifact verifier, target/index renders, workflow validation, and git diff --check. The recorded review decision then authorized the mechanical promotion to L1/stable. Stable status records bounded acceptance of this declared synthetic Benchmark Object; it does not expand its evidence, information-set, target, or interpretation boundaries.

title: Demixing and Rotational Projection Robustness Benchmark
text:
Demixing and rotational projection are separate tasks with separate grids, methods, targets, metrics, summaries and panels.
All 19 scenarios and three independent replicates are declared.
Generation, fitting/selection, frozen recovery and scoring boundaries are explicit.
Label and condition permutations are explicit negative-control paths.
Marginal reconstruction, decoding, subspace, plane, rate, derivative, tangential and covariance targets remain distinct.
Applicability precedes failure, and raw replicate rows are retained.
Exactly four byte-verifiable artifacts and authoritative commands are recorded.
Bounded results and interpretation limits are reconciled to the artifacts.
Final focused scientific re-review PASS is recorded.
Final focused implementation re-review PASS is recorded.
review-authorized mechanical promotion to L1/stable is complete.

title: P4-U01 — Linear-Gaussian Robustness Benchmark
text:
Across a bounded set of scalar linear-Gaussian state-space models (LGSSMs) with known synthetic ground truth, where are simple references, exact known-parameter inference, direct Gaussian conditioning, and a finite-grid plug-in variant applicable, robust, or observably brittle under their declared information sets?
This is a task-specific robustness study, not a general leaderboard. It compares performance only within the declared simulator, scenarios, metrics, splits, and information sets. It does not establish mechanism, causality, biological validity, real-data validity, or universal method superiority.



Each independent replicate generates separate train, validation, and test sequences from
\[
z_{t+1}=a z_t+w_t,\qquad w_t\sim\mathcal N(0,q),
\]
\[
x_t=z_t+v_t,\qquad v_t\sim\mathcal N(0,r),
\]
with stationary initialization \(z_1\sim\mathcal N(0,q/(1-a^2))\). The generator retains latent truth for scoring, but selection and inference do not receive it. The executable wraps the stable numerical routines in toy-models/linear-gaussian-inference-ladder.py; it does not edit or reinterpret the Phase 3 result. The manifest records this relationship as actual_executable_routine_reuse and freezes the reused source identity with SHA-256; verification rejects path, role, or digest drift.



Generation is a standalone stage that receives only a scenario identifier, replicate, split, and sequence index. It creates independent stationary LGSSM paths and observations, then applies only the scenario’s predeclared observation mask. It does not call selection, inference, or scoring.



The core-plus-stress grid contains five independent replicates per scenario and two sequences per split. It deliberately remains small enough for byte-level regeneration.







Scenario class
Predeclared variation




Transition stability
\(a\in\{0.60,0.85,0.97\}\) at fixed \(q=0.10,r=0.40,T=60\)


Process/observation noise ratio
process-dominant \((q,r)=(0.40,0.10)\) and observation-dominant \((0.025,0.80)\)


Sequence length
\(T=24\) and \(T=120\) against the \(T=60\) reference


Missing blocks
a contiguous half-open block \([28,48)\) in \(T=80\) sequences


Wrong parameters
true \((0.85,0.10,0.40)\) versus predeclared inference \((0.60,0.025,0.80)\)


Reset-boundary failure
an intentionally invalid filter continuation across two independent test sequences


Near-unit-root stress
\(a=0.99,q=0.02,r=0.40,T=120\)



The grid is fixed in manifest.json before interpretation. No scenario is tuned away after seeing a failure.



The wrong-parameter scenario freezes \((a,q,r)=(0.60,0.025,0.80)\) for inference while generation remains at \((0.85,0.10,0.40)\). The reset control deliberately carries a posterior across an independent sequence boundary and compares its first estimate with a correctly reset filter. The near-unit-root scenario tests long-horizon and numerical sensitivity at \(a=0.99\). These controls are retained even when they degrade performance.



Every scenario has five independent replicates, with two independently generated sequences in each split. A seed is mapped from the master seed, a SHA-256-derived scenario code, replicate, split code, and sequence index. The map does not depend on execution order.



Train and validation observations are available only to finite-grid selection. Frozen selected parameters are then passed to test inference. Test observations are used by the declared test-time information set; test latent truth is unavailable until the separate scoring stage. Whole independent sequences, not adjacent time points, define the partitions.




stationary mean: fixed zero reference;
persistence and open-loop: online observation-history references;
known-parameter Kalman filter: online posterior using observations through the current time;
fixed-interval RTS smoother: retrospective posterior using the complete declared interval;
direct batch Gaussian conditioning: exact bounded retrospective oracle;
finite-grid selected filter and smoother: parameters selected on train/validation observations and frozen before test inference;
wrong-parameter filter/smoother: scenario-specific misspecification controls; and
false-continuation filter: reset-boundary negative control, explicitly labelled as using an invalid cross-sequence history.

Online, retrospective, and oracle information sets are not pooled. A smoother can use future observations and therefore is not a deployable online competitor to a filter. The batch result is an implementation oracle, not a candidate with the same computational role.



The finite grid contains 27 predeclared tuples from \(a\in\{0.60,0.85,0.97\}\), \(q\in\{0.025,0.10,0.40\}\), and \(r\in\{0.10,0.40,0.80\}\). Each tuple is scored by mean train innovation NLL plus mean validation innovation NLL. Ties are broken lexicographically. The selection function accepts exactly four arrays—train observations, train masks, validation observations, and validation masks—and has no argument through which test data or latent truth can be supplied. Poison checks confirm that changing excluded test observations or latent truth leaves all scores and the selected tuple unchanged.



Inference receives observations, masks, sequence boundaries, and either known, selected, or predeclared-wrong parameters. Each sequence is normally invoked independently from its stationary prior. The false-continuation control is the sole deliberate boundary violation and is labelled with an invalid cross-sequence information history.



Only after inference outputs are frozen does scoring join test latent truth. Raw target metadata is metric-specific rather than inherited only from the method:







Metric
Raw target and definition

title: P4-U01 — Linear-Gaussian Robustness Benchmark
text:
Across a bounded set of scalar linear-Gaussian state-space models (LGSSMs) with known synthetic ground truth, where are simple references, exact known-parameter inference, direct Gaussian conditioning, and a finite-grid plug-in variant applicable, robust, or observably brittle under their declared information sets?
This is a task-specific robustness study, not a general leaderboard. It compares performance only within the declared simulator, scenarios, metrics, splits, and information sets. It does not establish mechanism, causality, biological validity, real-data validity, or universal method superiority.

title: P4-U02 — Static Linear Latent Recovery Benchmark
text:
Across a bounded grid of independent rank-two Gaussian-factor simulations and declared misspecification controls, when do mean and rank-matched projection references, ordinary PCA, probabilistic PCA (PPCA), bounded diagonal-noise factor analysis (FA), and known-parameter Gaussian references recover the different targets their criteria define, and where are they inapplicable, numerically nonconvergent, or observably brittle?
This is not a shared-target leaderboard. In particular, ordinary PCA is judged against the population principal subspace of the observable covariance, while FA loading recovery is judged against the common-loading structure only when the diagonal-residual model and the declared structural-identification diagnostic apply. Reconstruction, likelihood, covariance recovery, subspace recovery, uniqueness recovery, convergence, and leakage are separate tasks and are never collapsed into one score.



Each independent row is generated in ambient dimension \(p=8\) with latent rank \(q=2\):
\[
z_i\sim\mathcal N(0,I_2),\qquad
\epsilon_i\sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_\epsilon),\qquad
x_i=\Lambda z_i+\epsilon_i.
\]
The retained truth includes \(z\), \(\Lambda\), the common covariance \(C_{\mathrm{common}}=\Lambda\Lambda^\top\), residual covariance \(\Sigma_\epsilon\), observable covariance \(C=C_{\mathrm{common}}+\Sigma_\epsilon\), the loading subspace \(\operatorname{col}(\Lambda)\), and the rank-two population principal subspace of \(C\). These are not interchangeable targets.
Population parameters and latent arrays are available only to generation, scoring, and implementation-oracle checks. They are not supplied to lawful preprocessing, fitting, validation selection, or held-out recovery. The executable reuses the stable numerical definitions and routines in toy-models/static-linear-latent-recovery.py without editing the stable Toy Model or changing its scientific conclusions.


Three boundaries are recorded separately:

Structural identification applicability. For diagonal-noise FA, uniqueness and common-loading targets are eligible only when the residual covariance is diagonal and the displayed loading matrix passes the retained Anderson–Rubin-style sufficient row-deletion rank diagnostic. Loading columns remain equivalent under orthogonal rotation.
Finite-sample recovery. Principal angles and covariance errors describe one bounded fitted sample relative to known synthetic truth. Identification does not guarantee that these errors are small.
Optimizer convergence. The bounded EM implementation can reach its iteration limit or a numerical boundary. Convergence is a computational label, not proof of structural identification, population correctness, or global maximum likelihood; nonconvergence is not evidence that the population model class cannot represent the truth.





Generation receives only a scenario identifier, replicate identifier, split, and deterministic seed words. It produces independent train, validation, and test observations and retains truth in a separate scoring payload. Outlier contamination and residual correlation are applied only in their predeclared scenario classes. Generation does not call preprocessing, fitting, selection, recovery, or scoring.
The primary model uses the stable Toy Model’s deterministic rank-two loading basis and heterogeneous diagonal uniquenesses. Scenario-specific changes are fixed before outcome interpretation and are recorded in manifest.json.



The grid is a bounded core-plus-stress design rather than a complete factorial experiment. It covers every Phase 4 contract factor while keeping independent replicates and byte-level regeneration practical.

Changing one named scenario can also change the observable covariance, eigengap, or effective signal-to-noise ratio. Consequently, differences across scenario rows are conditional robustness observations, not isolated causal effects of one factor. Exact scenario values, split sizes, expected applicability, replicate count, and seed mapping are frozen in the manifest.




Fixed and seed-derived random rank-two projections show what rank matching alone can achieve without estimating a population target. There is exactly one random basis for each scenario-replicate.
Correlated residuals deliberately violate diagonal-noise FA. A fitted factor under this condition cannot be called a recovered common cause.
High-variance nuisance tests whether a variance-defined PCA target diverges from the unchanged loading target; correct PCA recovery is not a semantic error.
Near-zero uniqueness stresses positivity floors, boundary behavior, and finite iteration budgets.
Outliers violate the clean Gaussian law. The true clean parameters remain a nominal reference only, not the true distribution of contaminated data.
Pooled train/test preprocessing is explicitly invalid. Leakage is proved by dependence on poisoned test observations, not by whether one finite test score improves.

Failures are retained and labelled rather than tuned away.



Each of the 11 declared scenarios uses four independent deterministic replicates. Seed words include the master seed, a stable scenario code, replicate, split, and any sequence or baseline index needed by the generator. Mapping does not depend on execution order. Methods share a replicate’s generated data to support paired, target-specific comparisons, while different replicates use independent random streams.
One raw record is produced per scenario \(\times\) replicate \(\times\) method \(\times\) metric. Its value is computed from the metric-specific provenance declared under Scoring—test rows, validation rows, training optimization, population truth, or the train/test poison intervention as appropriate. Replicate identity is never discarded.



Train, validation, and test samples are generated independently. Training data fit means, lawful preprocessing, PCA/PPCA, and each bounded FA candidate. Validation observations select only among the predeclared FA floors and restarts. Test observations are used only by the frozen test-time recovery or likelihood calculation. Retained clean test signal and population parameters are joined only in the separate metric-specific scoring stage.
Lawful selection accepts restricted train/validation observation payloads. It has no capability to read test observations or any latent/population truth. Poison checks replace excluded test observations and retained latent arrays and require lawful fitted states, selected FA settings, and observation-only recoveries to remain unchanged. The pooled-scaling negative control is kept separate and explicitly labelled invalid.




Training mean: rank-zero reconstruction reference fitted on training observations.
Fixed rank-two projection: predeclared orthonormal compression reference; it is not fitted to outcomes.
Random rank-two projection: exactly one rank-two orthonormal basis is deterministically derived from the scenario and replicate seed, independently of that replicate’s generated observations. It is a rank-matched reference, not a validation-selected method. Across replicates, both the generated data and the seed-derived basis vary jointly; the replicate summary therefore does not isolate basis variability from sampling variability or average a family of bases within one replicate.
Ordinary covariance PCA: deterministic rank-two orthogonal projection fitted on training observations. Its population target is the leading rank-two eigenspace of the observable covariance under the declared preprocessing and Euclidean metric.
PPCA: the isotropic-residual Gaussian restriction \(C=WW^\top+\sigma^2I\). Its maximum-likelihood loading space is the PCA principal subspace, but it additionally supplies a Gaussian covariance, likelihood, and posterior mean. It is not general diagonal-noise FA, and its likelihood does not retroactively make ordinary PCA probabilistic.
Bounded diagonal-noise FA: a rank-two Gaussian model \(C=\Lambda\Lambda^\top+\operatorname{diag}(\psi)\) fitted by deterministic bounded EM candidates and validation selection. Loading columns are compared only through rotation-invariant subspace/common-covariance targets.
True-parameter Gaussian reference: uses known simulator parameters for likelihood and posterior reconstruction. It is an unavailable implementation/reference oracle, not a deployable fitted competitor. Under outlier contamination it is named and interpreted as a nominal clean Gaussian reference.

All lawful methods use the same frozen test observations. Population eigenspaces, loadings, covariances, uniquenesses, and latent scores are scoring truth or oracle inputs, never fitting information.



PCA and closed-form PPCA use the predeclared rank two and require no validation selection. Fixed/random projections are frozen before data generation. For FA, the training split fits every predeclared uniqueness-floor \(\times\) restart candidate; validation Gaussian NLL selects one candidate with a deterministic tie rule. The selected floor and restart are frozen before test recovery and scoring.
This finite candidate set is a bounded numerical procedure. It does not prove global optimization, and validation selection cannot turn a misspecified diagonal residual model into a correct one.



For reconstruction methods, recovery receives frozen preprocessing and fitted states plus test observations. PCA and projection baselines return Euclidean reconstructions in original coordinates. PPCA and FA return model-conditional Gaussian posterior-mean reconstructions. These are different estimators even at the same rank.
No method receives test latent truth. The true-parameter Gaussian reference is invoked through an explicitly oracle-labelled path. There is no temporal information set: observations are independent static rows, and their ordering has no scientific meaning.



Raw rows use metric-specific target metadata. The following task families remain separate:







Raw metric
Provenance, target, and interpretation




heldout_reconstruction_mse
Test observations and frozen reconstructions; original-coordinate observed reconstruction, including contaminated observations in outliers; not loading or covariance recovery


latent_signal_reconstruction_mse
Test clean common signal \(\Lambda z\) retained by the generator, compared with the fitted reconstruction after subtracting the declared population mean; defined for every method that returns a finite test reconstruction, including mean, fixed/random projection, PCA, PPCA, selected FA, and the true-parameter reference. The two scaled-PCA controls are applicable only in preprocessing_leakage. In outliers, observations and fitted reconstructions include contamination while the target remains the uncontaminated \(\Lambda z\), so the metric measures recovery of the clean simulated common contribution rather than reconstruction of the contaminated observation law


heldout_gaussian_nll
Test observations under a frozen PPCA, FA, or true-parameter Gaussian density; ordinary PCA and pure projections do not define this score. In outliers, this is a Gaussian score on contaminated observations, and the clean true-parameter model is only a nominal reference


covariance_relative_frobenius
Fitted model covariance versus population observable covariance; for outliers, the target is explicitly the nominal clean Gaussian covariance rather than the covariance of the contaminated law


principal_subspace_angle_max_degrees
Training-fitted PCA/PPCA space versus the population rank-two principal subspace of observable \(C\); the value combines fitted training output with population scoring truth, not test observations


loading_subspace_angle_max_degrees
Training/validation-selected FA loading space versus \(\operatorname{col}(\Lambda)\), or the exact reference against itself, only where the diagonal-residual and sufficient-rank identification conditions apply; population-truth scoring, not a test-split loss


uniqueness_rmse
Selected FA diagonal uniqueness versus population diagonal uniqueness only where the same identification conditions apply; the implementation emits RMSE, not uniqueness relative error


selected_validation_nll
Validation observations and the selected bounded FA candidate; a selection diagnostic, not held-out test performance


optimizer_iterations
Training optimization history of the selected FA candidate; a computational diagnostic. A run that reaches the bound is labelled nonconvergence


identification_applicable
Population scenario specification plus the sufficient rank diagnostic; a binary applicability record, not empirical recovery performance


preprocessing_test_poison_parameter_change
Difference between preprocessing/model parameters before and after deterministic test poisoning; uses training and test observations only for the declared leakage control and is not a candidate-method score



Provenance is therefore metric-specific: only the held-out reconstruction, clean-signal reconstruction, and Gaussian NLL metrics are direct test-row aggregates. Subspace, covariance, uniqueness, and identification metrics join fitted states to population truth; validation NLL comes from validation data; optimizer iterations come from training optimization; and the poison metric is a train/test perturbation diagnostic. The raw split/provenance field must be read with the metric and target rather than interpreted as saying that every numeric value is a test loss.
For observation-level losses, the relevant rows are first aggregated within one scenario-replicate. Every other metric likewise contributes at most one value for that scenario-replicate-method-metric key. diagnostics.json then reports median, q10, and q90 across the four independent replicate-level values, together with ok, failure, and applicability rates for each scenario \(\times\) method \(\times\) metric group. Test rows, features, and EM iterations are not treated as independent replicates. The random-projection row uses one seed-derived basis per scenario-replicate, so its across-replicate quantiles reflect joint data-and-basis variation. Unlike targets are not normalized, averaged, ranked, or pooled.
The FA loading subspace and common covariance are conceptually distinct: the former ignores loading magnitudes, whereas \(\Lambda\Lambda^\top\) retains them while remaining invariant to orthogonal loading rotations. This first bounded implementation directly emits the loading-subspace angle, observable-covariance error, and uniqueness error, but does not emit a separate common-covariance norm. Therefore it makes no numerical common-covariance-magnitude recovery claim; “common structure” in the reported results refers only to the declared loading-subspace target.
Likewise, residual off-diagonal error and uniqueness relative error are not raw metrics in this benchmark. Selected floor, restart, and convergence state are row metadata that identify the frozen FA candidate; convergence state is also used to assign failure labels. Candidate train NLL may be retained in bounded selection diagnostics for verification, but neither train NLL nor a standalone convergence flag is emitted as a scored raw metric. The only scored FA selection/computation metrics are selected_validation_nll and optimizer_iterations.



Every expected scenario \(\times\) replicate \(\times\) method \(\times\) metric row is retained with exactly one status:

ok: the target applies and the value is finite and valid;
nonconvergence: the bounded optimizer or numerical procedure did not meet its declared convergence contract;
invalid: the computation, covariance, preprocessing, or value is invalid, including the deliberate pooled-preprocessing control where appropriate;
inapplicable: the method does not define that likelihood, target, or identified quantity under the scenario.

Every non-ok row has a machine-readable reason. Structural-identification inapplicability, model misspecification, finite recovery error, and optimizer nonconvergence use different reasons and are not substituted for one another. Rows do not disappear because a method failed or a target does not apply.
